Special counsel Bob Spolzino and Councilman Hussain framed the board's role narrowly as checking for any impact on the town, of which there was none, and the amendment (noted as approved by 80%+ of lot owners) was adopted.

cases.name: Town Cleanup Day — Expenditures & Police/Highway Arrangements (April 26, 2025)

timeline.summary: The board approved expenditures (minor, historically a few hundred dollars up to a ~$1,000 max) and working arrangements with the police and highway departments for the town-wide cleanup day on Saturday, April 26, 2025 (9 AM-1 PM, rain or shine). The supervisor, liaison to the sustainability committee, described the resident-driven event and safety emphasis and credited volunteers. Councilman Milim thanked the board for reviving the event.

cases.name: License Agreement — Mount Pleasant PD Communication Equipment on Custis Water Tower

timeline.summary: The board approved a license agreement letting the Mount Pleasant Police Department install communication equipment on the Custis water tower to cover dead spots, and authorized the supervisor to sign. In a reciprocal arrangement Mount Pleasant PD will install North Castle's new two-way communication equipment at no cost, and pays the power costs; a formal license was needed due to an access easement. Adopted by voice vote.

cases.name: Sign Law Modernization — Work Session

timeline.summary: A work session (no vote) on updating the town's sign law to remove content-based restrictions and comply with the Supreme Court's Reed decision, resurrected after a year on the back burner. Debate centered on temporary and political signs: whether to require registration, how many temporary signs to allow per property, whether to permit longer display for special-event/250th banners, and whether designated sign areas or private-property placement is better. No decision was made; members agreed to submit written comments to Adam Kaufman (copying the full board and counsel) by roughly end of month, with another work session to follow.

cases.name: Licensing Agreement Request — Main Street Property (Michael)

timeline.summary: An applicant appeared to request a license agreement from the town relating to on-street parking spaces that cross a property line, referred to the board by the Town Planner. Because no license agreement had been drafted or submitted, the board tabled the matter, directing the applicant's attorney to prepare and submit the agreement for review and to verify with the Planning Department whether any existing variance runs with the property. Motion to table passed.

cases.name: Landmark Designation of the Eagle (Routes 128 & 22)

timeline.summary: The board received the Landmark Preservation Committee's recommendation to landmark the Eagle monument and surrounding streetscape at Routes 128 and 22 and scheduled a public hearing for May 14, 2025. Questions remain about whether to include the land (as opposed to just the monument), plus boundary/deed issues that may require a survey. The board voted to receive the recommendation (to be supplemented) and set the hearing date.

cases.name: Water District #4 Rehabilitation (IBM/Northwell Well)

timeline.summary: The board approved a series of actions for rehabilitating the IBM (Northwell) well in Water District No. 4: receiving the superintendent's memo, authorizing going to bid, approving an RFP for a replacement well pump, and approving WSP Engineering's proposal for project oversight. Supervisor Rende recused himself on this item due to its relation to the IBM community park. All motions carried.

cases.name: Payment Requisition #1 — Tony Casale Inc. (Kent Place / Verizon Parking Improvements)

timeline.summary: The board approved payment requisition No. 1 to Tony Casale Incorporated for the Kent Place Verizon parking plan improvements. Members noted the work is nearly finished and agreed it is time to start the conversation on the remainder of the parking lot/district. Motion carried.

cases.name: Liquor License — L&M Restaurant Inc., 405 Main Street

timeline.summary: The board received a new liquor license application from L&M Restaurant Inc. at 405 Main Street and waived the 30-day notice. Councilwoman DiGiacinto recused herself because the property is owned by the DiGiacinto family, citing it as an example of self-checking for ethics conflicts. Motion carried.

cases.name: Liquor License — Massarella Italian Steakhouse, 111 Bedford Road

timeline.summary: The board received a new liquor license application from Nezeraj Incorporated for Massarella Italian Steakhouse at 111 Bedford Road and waived the 30-day notice. Motion carried.

cases.name: Library RFP — Branding, Website Redesign & Event Calendar
cases.applicant: North Castle Public Library (Director Katherine Feeley)

timeline.summary: The board authorized the library director to issue an RFP for branding, website redesign and an event calendar system. Councilwoman DiGiacinto objected that the project was not in the 2025 budget and that unresolved safety issues (electrical panel, water/sewer, teen-room waterproofing) should take priority; staff reported those items are being addressed. The board approved authorizing the RFP on condition that the final RFP be reviewed through the town administrator's office and that any resulting bid/award return to the board for approval. Motion carried.

cases.name: Resolution Supporting Pedestrian Improvements Throughout the Town
cases.applicant: North Castle Parks & Recreation Advisory Board (Carl Hendricks)

timeline.summary: The board received a letter from the Parks & Recreation Advisory Board requesting sidewalks connecting downtown Armonk to Lombardy Park/the town pool, and adopted a broader resolution committing to pursue pedestrian improvements throughout all three hamlets in the most cost-effective way. Councilwoman DiGiacinto pressed that North White Plains has long sought Route 22 and Virginia Road sidewalks and urged a multi-year capital-priority approach. Motion carried.

cases.name: Special Counsel — Dichter Law for Con Edison Rate Case
cases.applicant: Joel R. Dichter / Dichter Law LLC

timeline.summary: The board authorized hiring Joel R. Dichter of Dichter Law LLC as special counsel to represent North Castle, alongside other Westchester municipalities, in the Consolidated Edison electric and gas rate case before the Public Service Commission. With about 39 municipalities joining, the per-town cost dropped from an estimated $5,000 to roughly $2,700. Members discussed potential conflicts if the firm represented other counties but were satisfied it would not. Motion carried.

cases.name: Westchester County Municipal Police Mobile Radio Program Agreement

timeline.summary: The board approved participation in the Westchester County Municipal Police Department's mobile radio program and authorized the supervisor to sign the agreement. Members noted police staff (Tom McCormick and Pete Simonson) had vetted and were satisfied with the terms. Motion carried.

cases.name: Metropolitan Regional Radio System (MRRS) Access Agreement with MTA Police

timeline.summary: The board approved the Metropolitan Regional Radio System (MRRS) systems access agreement with the MTA Police Department and authorized the supervisor to sign. Routine motion carried.

cases.name: License Agreement — Fisher Lane Meter Parking Lot (Westchester County)

timeline.summary: The board approved the license agreement with Westchester County for the Fisher Lane meter parking lot for the period April 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026, and authorized the supervisor to sign. Motion carried.

cases.name: Invasive Vine Mitigation Volunteer Program

timeline.summary: During public comment, resident Doug Mancinelli reported on the volunteer invasive-vine mitigation program launched three months ago, with eight successful events and 20+ volunteers at sites including the Erico property, Smith's Tavern and Sands Mill. He invited residents to upcoming events at the town pool. The board was enthusiastic; the Supervisor praised the effort and asked for a volunteer list so the town could send thank-you letters.

cases.name: Home Rule Request to Extend Hotel Occupancy Tax Legislation

timeline.summary: The board adopted a resolution making a home-rule request to the NYS Senate and Assembly to extend the hotel occupancy tax enabling legislation. Although the town currently has no hotel, keeping the legislation in place preserves the ability to collect the tax if a hotel is built in the future; proceeds are stipulated for road repair and maintenance. Adopted on a voice vote.

cases.name: Whale Ass Way Subdivision — Inspection Fee, Bonds and Townsend Burial Ground Easements

timeline.summary: The board acted on several Whale Ass Way items: accepting a KSCJ recommendation on the subdivision inspection fee and a stormwater performance bond, receiving a Singleton Davis & Singleton letter, and approving a declaration of easements/maintenance agreement for access to the Townsend burial ground plus the stormwater facilities construction/maintenance agreement, authorizing the Supervisor to sign (including form TP-584). Councilman Berra raised detailed questions about public access to the historic cemetery, insolvency notice provisions, and a rubber-stamp change clause. The declaration was adopted with a condition correcting the performance-guarantee amount to $230,298.48. All items passed on voice votes.

cases.name: Cassone Special Use Permit Amendment — Private Equestrian Use
cases.address: 22 Cowdery Drive and 50 Round Hill Road, Armonk, NY

timeline.summary: The board received a special-use-permit application from Mary Lou Cassone to amend a 1992 permit recognizing continued private equestrian use alongside the principal dwelling, and scheduled a public hearing for May 14, 2025. On the Town Attorney's advice, it also voted to refer the matter to the North Castle and Westchester County planning boards and to declare the Town Board lead agency for SEQRA. Passed on voice votes.

cases.name: Mianus River Gorge — Planning Board Fee Waiver Request

timeline.summary: The nonprofit Mianus River Gorge requested a waiver/reduction of the ~$300 planning board filing fees (not the professional escrow) for a site-plan application to renovate office space. The board debated at length whether to grant it: the Supervisor and Councilwoman DiGiacinto objected to acting without a townwide policy and criteria for nonprofit fee waivers, while another member argued fairness favored granting a reduction for a worthy nonprofit. The board voted to table the item and asked Town Planner Adam Kaufman (via the Administrator) to draft a fee-waiver policy for board review.

cases.name: Water/Sewer Department Memo on Fire District Agreements — Referral to Town Attorney

timeline.summary: The board received a memo dated April 15, 2025 from the water/sewer department director regarding fire district agreements and referred the matter to the Town Attorney. Adopted on a voice vote with no substantive debate.

cases.name: Wetland Mitigation Performance/Monitoring Bonds — Bella, Kamar and Rogel Residences
cases.address: 3 Seymour Place West; 75 Hickory Kingdom Road; 18 Caroline Place

timeline.summary: On KSCJ Consulting recommendations, the board established wetland mitigation bonds for three residential projects: a performance bond plus five-year monitoring/maintenance bond for the Bella residence (3 Seymour Place West), the same for the Kamar residence (75 Hickory Kingdom Road), and a five-year monitoring/maintenance bond for the Rogel residence (18 Caroline Place). Each item passed on a routine voice vote.

cases.name: Kent Place / Verizon Parking Lot Improvements — Payment Requisition No. 4 (Tony Casal Inc.)
cases.address: Kent Place / Verizon parking lot, Armonk

timeline.summary: On a KSCJ recommendation, the board approved payment requisition No. 4 to Tony Casal Inc. for the Kent Place/Verizon parking lot improvements. Members reported the final asphalt layer was laid that day, with only lighting and some fencing remaining, and praised the contractor and town staff (Kevin, Jamie, Joe Chimelli of Kellard). The Supervisor also flagged advancing the broader parking-district plan via a public informational work session. Adopted on a voice vote.

cases.name: Jewish Board of Family and Children Services — Cycle of Support Cycling Event
cases.applicant: Jewish Board of Family and Children Services

timeline.summary: The board approved a request from the Jewish Board of Family and Children Services to use town roads and parks for a 'Cycle of Support' cycling event on Sunday, September 14. Per an uploaded note from Police Lieutenant McCormick, roughly five police officers (subject to adjustment) will provide presence, paid for by the applicant. Adopted on a voice vote.

cases.name: Washington-Rochambeau Revolutionary Route (W3R-US) 'Victory Towns' Membership

timeline.summary: The board considered joining the W3R-US 'Victory Towns' membership program at either a $2,200 or $4,500 level; resident Ed Woodyard urged the higher tier so the Supervisor could attend a Philadelphia event. The Supervisor and Councilwoman DiGiacinto viewed the membership as essentially a donation with little tangible benefit, preferring instead to fund the town's own historical marker/plaque (e.g., at Sands Mill) using suggested commemorative language. The item was tabled.

cases.name: EDR Contract Amendment — Sewer District No. 2 Wastewater Treatment Plant Upgrade
cases.address: Sewer District No. 2 Wastewater Treatment Plant

timeline.summary: The board considered an amendment to EDR's June 2020 contract for the Sewer District No. 2 wastewater plant upgrade, adding roughly $161,000 (~60%) to accommodate Westchester County Health Department backwash-filtration requirements that forced a redesign (additional pumping station, revised drawings) over five years. Superintendent Sal gave a detailed presentation explaining the non-mandated nitrogen-reduction enhancement and why costs rose. Councilman Berra pressed for a breakdown showing the increase was 'fair and equitable,' while the Supervisor expressed full confidence in Sal and the rest of the board favored proceeding. The amendment was adopted by roll call, with EDR to still provide a cost breakdown for the file.

cases.name: Award of Bids for Highway Materials

timeline.summary: On a request from Highway General Foreman Jamie Norris, the board awarded annual bids for highway materials laid in place — asphalt milling/disposal, concrete, winter highway materials, aggregate stone, guardrails, catch basins and pavement markings — and authorized the Supervisor to sign. Described as routine annually bid items; adopted on a voice vote.

cases.name: Town Pool Concession Services — R&A Ice Cream (2025 Season)

timeline.summary: The board approved a proposal from R&A Ice Cream to operate the town pool concession for the 2025 season and authorized the Supervisor to sign. Members discussed upcoming pool capital work — deck replacement and gutter/filter/pump improvements to be bid via KSCJ and Macri and performed after the season — and confirmed the pool remains on schedule to open on time. Adopted on a voice vote.

cases.name: KSCJ Engineering Services — Clove Road Baseball Fields
cases.address: 10 Clove Road / Corporate Clove Road, North White Plains, NY

timeline.summary: The board approved a KSCJ proposal for engineering services for the baseball fields at Clove Road and authorized the Supervisor to sign. The Supervisor thanked applicant Bob Kandria for his patience and credited cost-saving collaboration with DeRosa Sports and Kellard's Joe Chimelli, noting drainage improvements and the possibility of reusing turf-project spoil material from Community Park to lower costs. Adopted on a voice vote; work anticipated to begin by the end of the season.

cases.name: Tree Code Amendment — Conservation Board Work Session
cases.applicant: Conservation Board (John Krupa, Adam Barnett, co-chairs)

timeline.summary: The Conservation Board presented proposed amendments to the town's tree code: clarifying the definitions of 'clearing' versus 'thinning,' tightening permit triggers (down to three trees or 25% of a parcel), simplifying regulated-setback language, making compliance explicitly the homeowner's responsibility, and raising the maximum fine from $1,000 to $2,000 (double for significant/wetland trees). Debate centered on whether higher fines would deter violations (Building Inspector Melillo argued judges rarely impose meaningful tree fines and the town sees few complaints), whether contractors could be held liable, and how to better detect unpermitted cutting. The board reached no decision but authorized Town Planner Adam Kaufman to keep refining the local-law language, with strong consensus that a public education campaign (mailers, video, outreach to realtors and contractors) is the most important component. Roland (Town Attorney) noted the fine must be worded 'up to' to preserve judicial discretion, so the flat-$2,000 draft was not viable as written.

cases.name: Speeding and Stop-Sign Concerns on Nethermont Avenue, North White Plains

timeline.summary: During public comment a North White Plains resident raised dangerous speeding and stop-sign running on Nethermont Avenue, asking for speed bumps or cameras. Supervisor Rende reported the police chief will reinstall a speed sign and is recommending reducing the town-road speed limit in North White Plains from 30 to 25 mph, and agreed to ask for extra patrols. The board asked the chief and traffic sergeant to evaluate options; members noted speed humps/tables versus bumps and rumble strips, and that state law and bus routes limit where bumps are allowed.

cases.name: Casson Equestrian Special Use Permit Amendment (1992 SUP)
cases.address: 40 Cowdery Park Drive and 50 Round Hill Road (Conyers Farm)
cases.applicant: Marianne Casson (James G. Dabini & Associates, attorneys)

timeline.summary: The applicant sought to amend a 1992 private-stable special use permit (up to 41 horses) to formally recognize continued equestrian use alongside the principal dwelling built in 2006 — a conversion that was never made when the house was constructed, voiding the 1992 SUP under its condition 22. The building inspector's May 13 letter flagged multiple property deficiencies and the planning board had not yet issued its recommendation, so the board could only condition any SUP on compliance. Neighbors (Lauren Pincus, Fred Cohen) and members raised sharp concerns that the property is being used commercially (renting stalls, up to 30 horses under lease, riders on the roads, manure/setback issues), which the town code and 1992 permit appear to prohibit; counsel disputed the meaning of the 'no commercial leasing' clause. Because recognizing the residence-plus-equestrian use would require a use variance from the Zoning Board, the board adjourned the public hearing to a date uncertain to let the applicant address planning-board items, pursue the variance, and cure the building deficiencies (roughly two months).

cases.name: Landmark Designation of the North Castle Eagle
cases.address: Corner of Route 128 and Route 22, Armonk

timeline.summary: The Landmark Preservation Committee asked the board to landmark the restored Armonk 'Eagle,' requesting the surrounding streetscape (fence-to-Eagle) as it had done conceptually for the gazebo. On the advice of counsel, citing unresolved legal issues over the underlying land, the board chose to landmark the Eagle sculpture itself — as it had with the gazebo and barber pole — without the land. The public hearing was held and closed, and the board unanimously adopted the designation of the Eagle alone, leaving possible streetscape/land questions for future investigation.

cases.name: Armonk has a Heart — Art Show Signs & Sculptures (Sept/Oct)
cases.applicant: Friends of the North Castle Public Library / Armonk Outdoor Art Show (Nancy Rosner)

timeline.summary: The board approved a request from the Friends of the Library and the Armonk Outdoor Art Show to place 12 decorated fiberglass heart sculptures and temporary signage around town for September (and possibly October) leading up to the Sept. 27-28 art show. Sculptures will be sponsored by local businesses, painted by local artists, and auctioned to benefit the North Castle Public Library. Members were enthusiastic, noting the effort drives visitors into downtown businesses; the board approved the temporary installation unanimously.

cases.name: Cancellation of the July 9, 2025 Town Board Meeting

timeline.summary: The board voted unanimously to cancel the July 9, 2025 meeting, moving to a single July meeting mirroring its longstanding single-August-meeting practice, on the recommendation of the Town Clerk's office.

cases.name: Policy — Waiver of Application Fees for Not-for-Profit Organizations

timeline.summary: Staff drafted a broad policy allowing not-for-profit organizations to seek waivers of town application fees, prompted by a recent request. The board declined to adopt it, voting on a motion to not approve. Members felt the town has never needed such a policy (only occasional tent/alcohol-permit waivers), that a $300 planning-board fee is not a genuine hardship for an organization building an addition, and that a broad policy would invite a flood of waiver requests; some were open only to a much narrower policy limited to demonstrated financial hardship. A related tabled fee-waiver request was left tabled rather than acted on.

cases.name: IBM Community Park Artificial Turf Field — DEC Letter & Soil Fill Characterization

timeline.summary: The board received a May 2, 2025 letter from the NYS DEC and a May 12, 2025 preliminary soil fill materials characterization from Hydro Environmental Solutions for the IBM Community Park artificial turf field improvements. The Supervisor noted the excavated material was confirmed clean and stable and can be reused at other town sites (Clove Field, Quarry Heights park), saving carting and fill costs by using town staff and equipment.

cases.name: Kent Place Parking Lot (Former Verizon Property) — Payment Req. #3 & Change Orders
cases.address: Kent Place parking lot (former Verizon property), Armonk

timeline.summary: The board approved Payment Requisition No. 3 to Tony Casale Incorporated for the Kent Place parking lot / former Verizon property improvements (on the revised requisition with sales tax removed), and separately approved change orders 1-3 and 6-9 per a KSCJ Consulting letter, authorizing the Supervisor to sign. Members noted the finished library-area work looks excellent, and discussed advancing a parking-district concept and interim pothole patching for the adjacent business-owned lot.

cases.name: Water District / Board of Fire Commissioners Agreements (Districts 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9)
cases.applicant: Town Water Districts / North Castle & Armonk Fire Districts

timeline.summary: The board approved, by unanimous voice votes, a series of agreements between town Water Districts (Nos. 1, 2, 4, 5, 8 and 9) and the respective Boards of Fire Commissioners (North Castle Fire District No. 1 and Armonk Fire District No. 2), authorizing the Supervisor to sign each. It also approved a license agreement for parking on a portion of roadway at 111 Lafayette Avenue, North White Plains.

cases.name: North Castle Pool and Tennis Club — Engineering Services Proposals
cases.address: North Castle Pool and Tennis Club, Armonk
cases.applicant: KSCJ Consulting and Engineering Services; Grossfeld Macri Consulting Engineers PC

timeline.summary: The board approved two professional-services proposals for the North Castle Pool and Tennis Club — one with KSCJ Consulting and Engineering Services and one with Grossfeld Macri Consulting Engineers PC for structural engineering services — and authorized the Supervisor to sign the agreements.

cases.name: Renewal Agreement — J. O'Connell Associates Grant Writing Services

timeline.summary: The board approved a renewal agreement with J. O'Connell & Associates for grant-writing services and authorized the Supervisor to sign. Administrator Kevin Foley reported the firm secured an approximately $450,000 Assault Dome grant, is aggressive, and is worth continuing despite some unsuccessful applications; members asked for follow-up on why some grants weren't awarded.

cases.name: New Capital Project Fund and Seward District Fund-Balance Transfer for EDR Contract

timeline.summary: On a memo from the Finance Director, the board voted to create a new capital project fund and to approve use of Seward District's fund balance of $161,300 to fund the amendment to EDR's contract (previously approved). After some procedural confusion over whether to receive and approve separately, the board consolidated it into a single amended motion that passed on a voice vote. Supervisor Rende urged developing an actual three- to five-year capital improvement plan to prioritize future spending.

cases.name: General Fund Loan to Water District 4 for New Well Building and Site Work

timeline.summary: The board received a memo and approved an internal loan from the town's general fund to Water District 4 to finance a prefab turnkey well building and site work, repaid with interest at the town's earning rate rather than issuing an outside bond, saving an estimated $55,000. The plan is to eventually roll this short-term loan into a larger long-term bond tied to the Airport Campus/Water District 8 interconnection to Westchester Joint Water Works. Motions to receive and approve both passed; the approval motion included a caveat that the loan remains callable if the town needs the funds, though counsel confirmed the town retains that right regardless. Members debated liquidity risk given the project could take 1.5 to 5+ years due to Health Department delays.

cases.name: Bid Award — Water District 4 Well Rehabilitation Project (Weston & Sampson)
cases.applicant: Weston & Sampson CMR Inc. (DBA SB Church)

timeline.summary: The board awarded a bid to Weston & Sampson for rehabilitation of an overburden (gravel-pack) well in Water District 4 and authorized the Supervisor to sign the agreement, at a cost of roughly $67,787. The superintendent explained the roughly 10-year maintenance cycle needed to restore the well's declining yield (down from 350 to 230 gallons per minute). Motion made and seconded, passed on a voice vote.

cases.name: Fourth Two-Year Extension of Special Use Permit — Park Place Long-Term Parking Structure
cases.applicant: Park Place, 11 New King Street, LLC (Neil Alexander, Cuddy & Feder)

timeline.summary: The board received a letter and adopted a resolution granting a fourth two-year extension (to July 2027) of the special use permit for a mechanized long-term parking structure. The applicant explained the delay was due to water-service issues with Westchester County that are now largely resolved, with the county bringing public water along New King Street. Counsel noted public water (not a well) is required partly because nearby wells were contaminated and for fire prevention. Motion passed on a voice vote.

cases.name: Special Use Permit Extension — Gateway Residential Redevelopment (former Mariani Gardens)
cases.applicant: NCD Acquisitions (Jeffrey Buss, Smith Buss & Jacobs LLP)

timeline.summary: The applicant requested a second one-year extension of the special use permit for the Gateway multi-family redevelopment at the former Mariani Gardens site. Instead of a full year, the board granted only a short extension to July 23, 2025, conditioned on the applicant paying delinquent taxes (a $49,016.82 payment including penalties was made the day of the meeting) and bringing the eyesore vacant property into compliance with the town's property-maintenance code (Chapter 241) — including removing stored rock/equipment, filling the excavation, and mowing. Supervisor Rende disclosed campaign donations from LLC members but affirmed impartiality. The motion, framed by special counsel Spolzino and moved by DiGiacinto, passed 4-1 on a roll-call vote with Councilman Berra opposed.

cases.name: Liquor License Notice and Waiver of 30-Day Notice — Cuckoo Armonk Inc.

timeline.summary: The board received notice of a new liquor license application for Cuckoo Armonk Inc. and waived the 30-day notice requirement. Counsel confirmed no further action was required beyond the notification. Motion passed on a voice vote.

cases.name: Subdivision Construction Performance Bond and Inspection Fees — Rolling Hill Subdivision
cases.applicant: 111 Round Hill Road Realty, LLC (per KSCJ Consulting recommendation)

timeline.summary: On a recommendation from KSCJ Consulting, the board approved establishing a subdivision construction performance bond for a common driveway and subdivision inspection fees for the Rolling Hill Subdivision. Motion made and seconded, passed on a voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Summer Camp Bus Lease Agreement — Byram Hills Central School District

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign a summer camp bus lease agreement with the school district effective June 30 through August 8, 2025. Motion made and seconded, passed on a voice vote.

cases.name: Summer Camp Facilities Agreement — Chittenden Middle School and Wampus Elementary

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign an agreement with the Byram Hills Central School District for use of H.C. Chittenden Middle School and Wampus Elementary School for the town summer camp from late June through the first week of August 2025. Supervisor Rende and DiGiacinto thanked the district as great partners, noting the camp would be impossible without the buildings. Motion passed on a voice vote.

cases.name: Police Training Approval — Detective Steven Vitolo, Homicide Seminar

timeline.summary: As a late addition brought in that morning by the chief, the board approved Detective Steven Vitolo attending the Colonel Henry F. Williams Homicide Seminar in Albany, September 21-26, 2025. Members noted the town has sent detectives to this training before. Milim briefly questioned not having seen the email but voted in favor. Motion passed on a voice vote.

cases.name: Receipt of 2024 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) — Bonadio Group
cases.applicant: Bonadio Group (Michael Connolly, manager); Comptroller Abbas

timeline.summary: Auditor Michael Connolly presented the ACFR and required communication letter for the year ended December 31, 2024, giving an unmodified (clean) opinion consistent with prior years. He explained the government-wide net-position deficit is driven by a $77M OPEB liability and that fund-level balance is a positive $33.6M, and noted implementation of GASB 101 (compensated absences). No difficulties or disagreements with management were reported. The board voted to accept the audit and thanked Comptroller Abbas and his team; staff noted continued GFOA recognition.

cases.name: Agenda Item B — Tabled pending report of law-enforcement activity

timeline.summary: The Supervisor asked to table an unspecified agenda item (Item B) because law enforcement had been involved at the location the previous night and no clear report was yet available. He said it was in the community's best interest to take no action. The board voted to table it.

cases.name: KSCJ Consulting recommendation — Eisenberg Residence, 47 Windmill Road: release wetland mitigation bond and extend monitoring/maintenance bond to 2030

timeline.summary: On the recommendation of the town's consultant KSCJ, the board acted on the Eisenberg Residence project to release the wetland mitigation bond and extend the five-year monitoring and maintenance bond through May 2030. Approved without substantive discussion.

cases.name: Adoption of revised Workplace Violence and Sexual Harassment Policies
cases.applicant: Town Administrator Kevin / Labor Counsel (Bond Schoeneck)

timeline.summary: The board considered two Labor-Counsel-drafted policy rewrites (workplace violence and sexual harassment) that update long-outdated existing policies. A sharp dispute erupted over process and substance: Councilman Berra had submitted track-changes comments only that day and wanted an executive session with Labor Counsel before adopting, and Councilman Milim wanted to 'get it right' rather than adopt and re-issue. The Supervisor and Councilmembers Hussain and DiGiacinto argued to adopt now and amend later, deferring to the experts, with Rende frustrated by repeated last-minute edits. The board voted 4-1 to TABLE both policies (Milim, Berra, DiGiacinto, Hussain aye; Rende no), to revisit in executive session with Labor Counsel at the next meeting and vote at the following meeting, with all changes to be circulated in advance under privilege.

cases.name: Resolution designating town-owned parcel 122.16-2 (5 General Heath, North White Plains) as dedicated open space

timeline.summary: Championed by Councilwoman DiGiacinto, the resolution dedicates a small (0.37-acre) town-owned steep-slope parcel contiguous to the historically significant Miller Hill/Miller Park as protected open space, to help guard against erosion and development impacts near the historic site. She noted the negligible tax impact. The board expressed unanimous support and adopted it.

cases.name: Amendment to agreement with WSP USA Inc. (Jan 13, 2021) — construction engineering for Water District No. 4 new well

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign an amendment to the 2021 WSP USA agreement for construction engineering on the Water District No. 4 new-well project, paid from the water district No. 4 operating budget. Water/sewer superintendent Sal noted the long-running project (permitting began years before 2021) is now in its 'home stretch.' Approved.

cases.name: MOU with Byram Hills School District — School Resource (Police) Officer services, 2025-2026 school year
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle / Byram Hills School District

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign a memorandum of understanding with the Byram Hills School District for the town to provide School Resource Officer (SRO) police services for the 2025-2026 school year. Approved without substantive debate.

cases.name: Appointment of Michael Calderola as Police Officer

timeline.summary: The Chief formally recommended Michael Calderola, a licensed master social worker and Coast Guard Auxiliary member, for appointment to the budgeted position of police officer effective June 28, 2025, following a thorough background investigation. The board voted by voice ('all in favor, aye') to approve the appointment, after which the Supervisor administered the oath of office. Rende noted the appointment finally brings the department to its long-budgeted staffing level after years stuck around 28 officers. Calderola will attend the Westchester County Police Academy beginning July 7.

cases.name: State Legislative Update — DOT Road Funding & End-of-Session Report (Sen. Mayer, Asm. Burdick)
cases.applicant: Sen. Shelly Mayer; Asm. Chris Burdick

timeline.summary: State Senator Shelly Mayer and Assemblyman Chris Burdick reported securing $26.5 million in additional DOT funding to rebuild Route 120 ($11M) and repave Route 22 from Kensico Dam to Route 120 ($15.5M), moved up into the current five-year capital plan after years of the town pressing the state. They also reviewed budget wins on EMS (a county-led planning process and EMS costs excluded from the tax cap), education aid (updated Westchester regional cost index, foundation aid, universal school meals, cell-phone ban), environment funding, and the Con Edison rate-case intervention. This was an informational presentation, not a board vote. Rende publicly apologized for being 'heated' in prior DOT meetings and thanked the legislators and the police chief for driving the results.

cases.name: Revolutionary War 250th Committee — Art Contest & Events Update
cases.applicant: North Castle Revolutionary War 250 Steering Committee (Ed Woodyard, Marion Hamilton)

timeline.summary: Committee members Ed Woodyard and Marion Hamilton updated the board during public comment on 250th-anniversary programming, thanking the town and Highway Department for retrieving a time capsule. They launched a town-wide original art contest (submissions July 4 through January 15, 2026, juried with prizes and a 2026 exhibit) and a companion library history exhibit. No board action was required. Milim asked whether AI-generated or digitally manipulated art must be disclosed; the committee confirmed disclosure is required per the contest specifications.

cases.name: Resolution Authorizing Health Dept Permit Application — Commercial Wading Pool Pump Modification

timeline.summary: The board ratified/adopted a resolution authorizing a permit application to the Westchester County Department of Health for modification of the existing commercial wading (kiddie) pool, specifically for the pool pump change. Approved by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Payment Requisition #1 — Engineered Fluid Inc., Water District #4 New Well Building

timeline.summary: The board approved Payment Requisition No. 1 to Engineered Fluid Incorporated for work on the Water District #4 new well building. Water/Sewer superintendent 'Sal' was present to answer questions; none were raised. Rende reflected that the roughly 350-gallon-per-minute well project has taken years but is an important move, and approved it by voice vote.

cases.name: Receipt of Email Rescinding Owner Consent — Be Yourself Spa Special Use Permit (99 Lafayette Ave)

timeline.summary: The board accepted receipt of an email from the 99 Lafayette Avenue property owner (May 99 Holdings, LLC) rescinding the owner's consent for the Be Yourself Spa special use permit application. Handled by motion and voice vote as a receipt item, with no substantive discussion.

cases.name: Kellart Sessions Recommendation — Wetland Mitigation & Maintenance Bond, Nassau Massar Residence
cases.address: 8 Cole Drive and 24 Davis Drive, Armonk

timeline.summary: The board received a recommendation from Kellart Sessions Consulting regarding a new wetland mitigation bond, to be followed by a maintenance plan bond, for the Nassau Massar residence project at 8 Cole Drive and 24 Davis Drive. Handled as a receipt item by motion and voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Film Permit — YDEO Productions Inc., Cranberry Lake Preserve

timeline.summary: The board approved a film permit application for YDEO Productions Incorporated to film a feature film at Cranberry Lake Preserve from July 16 to July 18, 2025. Approved by voice vote; Rende joked he had no idea what the acronym stood for.

cases.name: Appointment of Stephanie Paul — Hourly Librarian, North Castle Public Library

timeline.summary: The board approved the appointment of Stephanie Paul as an hourly librarian at the North Castle Public Library, effective July 10, 2025. Approved by voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Resignation of Charles Hornbeck III — Highway Department

timeline.summary: The board accepted the letter of resignation of Charles Hornbeck III from the Highway Department, effective June 28, 2025, by voice vote. Rende asked Town Administrator Kevin how long the employee had served and pressed to ensure an exit interview is conducted, saying exit interviews should be a standing policy.

cases.name: Appointment of Shruthi Franklin — Records Digitization Intern, Town Clerk's Office

timeline.summary: The board appointed Shruthi Franklin to a records digitization intern position in the Town Clerk's office, effective June 30, 2025. Approved by voice vote. Rende asked that the position's goals and accomplishments be documented so the board can evaluate the value of such temporary/intern roles in future.

cases.name: County Executive Update & ConEd Rate-Hike Intervention

timeline.summary: County Executive Ken Jenkins addressed the board on the July storms and Route 22/I-287 flooding, an emergency-operations debrief with the town, a projected ~$25M shortfall in the county's $2.5B budget, the Banksville Road bid, the airport main-terminal modernization RFP, and the county's intervention in the ConEd (and forthcoming NYSEG) delivery-rate cases. Barbara DiGiacinto thanked him for the county's seat at the table on the 'jaw-dropping' proposed 2026 delivery-rate hikes and urged residents/ratepayers to file comments before the November deadline. No vote; this was an informational presentation and advocacy discussion.

cases.name: Receipt of Resident Letter on Short-Term Rental at 31 Washington Avenue
cases.applicant: Neighboring property owners (Tan Nguyen and others)

timeline.summary: The board voted to receive a letter and petition from neighbors of 31 Washington Avenue documenting years of quality-of-life problems (all-night parties, noise, reckless driving, blocked hydrant and shared driveway, harassment) from an out-of-state owner's Airbnb operation with up to 40+ guests. Because North Castle has no short-term-rental regulation, the board noted Town Planner Adam Kaufman and counsel are beginning to draft an STR law, and a public hearing will be held before any law is adopted. The letter was received by voice vote; the underlying legislation was not yet discussed on its merits.

cases.name: Gateway (former Mariani Gardens) — Third One-Year Special Use Permit Extension
cases.address: Former Mariani Gardens site, RMFDA district, Armonk

timeline.summary: The board considered a third one-year extension of the special use permit for the Gateway attached/multifamily development on the former Mariani Gardens site. After extended debate over the property's eyesore condition, rocks allegedly stored in a floodplain, past tax delinquency, and how long the extension should be, the board went into executive session for advice of counsel. It returned and conditioned the one-year renewal on the applicant's written commitments to maintain the property in current condition, keep secure/locked access, and pay taxes timely. On a roll-call vote the extension carried with Milim, Hussain and Supervisor Rende in favor, DiGiacinto opposed, and Berra abstaining. Rende disclosed that principals of the ownership had contributed to his campaign but said it did not preclude a fair vote.

cases.name: Sands Mill Historic Site — Vegetation Clearing Contract
cases.applicant: North Castle Historical Society / Demo Landscape LLC

timeline.summary: The board approved a request from the North Castle Historical Society to have Demo Landscape LLC clear dead trees and invasive vines from the Major Andre / Sands Mill historic site at no cost to the town, with the contractor providing insurance naming the town as additional insured and indemnity. This is phase one, done by hand with no heavy machinery and staying within the stone-wall boundaries to protect any wetland buffer, with a phase-two review by the Conservation Board to follow. Approved by voice vote; the board praised the volunteer effort.

cases.name: Wetland Mitigation Bond Change — Rogel Project, 18 Caroline Place

timeline.summary: The board accepted an amended recommendation from KSCJ Consulting regarding the five-year wetland mitigation, monitoring and maintenance bond for the Rogel residential project at 18 Caroline Place. Town Planner Adam Kaufman clarified that going forward the planting/completion bond will only be required in specific circumstances (e.g., off-season plantings or illegal wetland disturbance not tied to a certificate of occupancy) rather than across the board, since the CO itself motivates completion. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Accept $1,000 Donation from Byram Hills Preschool Association
cases.applicant: Byram Hills Preschool Association / Superintendent of Recreation and Parks

timeline.summary: The board approved a request from the Superintendent of Recreation and Parks to accept a $1,000 donation from the Byram Hills Preschool Association. Approved by voice vote with thanks for the donation.

cases.name: Armonk Cider and Donut Festival / BHPA Carnival Permit
cases.applicant: Armonk Chamber of Commerce and Byram Hills Preschool Association

timeline.summary: The board approved a request from the Armonk Chamber of Commerce and the Byram Hills Preschool Association to hold the Armonk Cider and Donut Festival, featuring Jamie's 5K Run for Love and the BHPA Carnival, on Sunday, September 14, 2025. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: Town Hall Project — Release of Request for Expression of Interest (RFEI)
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (memo from special counsel Robert Spolzino)

timeline.summary: The centerpiece and most contested item: the board voted to release an RFEI inviting responders to propose options for consolidating town offices, a new police station, and an OCA-compliant court (potentially including public-private-partnership and mixed-use concepts) on the town-owned campus or another hamlet site. Supervisor Rende framed it as a no-cost, non-binding fact-finding exercise following the earlier 333 Main Street condemnation hearings, and stressed any real decision would go to a public referendum. Numerous residents (Keith Rosenthal, Andrew Lester, Mike Shaliro, Marilyn Huck, Sue Shimer, Sharon Tombach, others) objected to the process, the summer timing, non-disclosure of the document, traffic/density concerns, and preservation of the historic district. On separate motions the board received counsel's memo, added the item to the agenda, and voted by roll call to send the RFEI out July 24; it carried 4-1 with DiGiacinto opposed. The privileged counsel memo was read aloud after the board waived privilege.

cases.name: Peak Power Systems — Emergency Generator Service Extension (Water & Sewer)

timeline.summary: The board approved a proposal from Peak Power Systems Inc. to extend annual emergency generator service for the 15 associated units in the Water and Sewer Department from August 1, 2025 through August 15, 2026. Approved by voice vote.

cases.name: D&B Engineers — Water District 8 to District 4 Interconnect Proposal

timeline.summary: The board conceptually approved a proposal from D&B Engineers and Architects for engineering services to interconnect Water District No. 8 (the airport-campus water main extension) into Water District No. 4, subject to the town attorney's review of the forthcoming contract before the supervisor signs. Approved by voice vote to keep the project moving as the developer's side of the water-main work is already underway.

cases.name: Ethics Code Amendment — Legal Review and Public Hearing Status

timeline.summary: Raised under liaison updates, the board discussed the stalled ethics-code amendment proposed by the Ethics Board, on which special counsel had opined a portion was legally invalid/overreaching. Because a substantive change requires re-drafting and a new public hearing (with the existing hearing to be closed), the board set a deadline for members to submit comments to counsel by the August 13 meeting and agreed to take it up in executive session then. DiGiacinto objected that airing the matter under a liaison update, tied to an executive-session request not on the agenda, was 'not fair.' No vote taken; direction only.

cases.name: High School Intern Presentation — Jenny Hsu 250th Anniversary Essay
cases.applicant: Town Clerk's Office / North Castle High School Internship Program

timeline.summary: Intern Jenny Hsu, working through the Town Clerk's office, read an original essay on North Castle's role in the American Revolution written for the NY Association of Towns' 250th-anniversary documentary project. Board members praised the essay warmly and the Supervisor asked her to return to read it during the town's 2026 celebration and to place a copy in the town time capsule. Ceremonial item with no vote.

cases.name: United Hardware & Convenience — Special Use Permit for Outdoor Propane Sales

timeline.summary: The board voted to receive United Hardware's special-use-permit application to sell/exchange small propane tanks from a caged container, refer it to the county planning board, and schedule a public hearing for September 10, 2025. Town Planner Adam Kaufman noted the applicant has not yet completed all required documents and staff are following up. Motion carried.

cases.name: Letter from Board of Fire Commissioners — North Castle South Fire District No. 1
cases.applicant: Board of Fire Commissioners, North Castle South Fire District No. 1

timeline.summary: The board received an August 4 letter in which the fire district refused to sign an agreement, cited aging Water District 1 infrastructure, and stated it would not use newly installed hydrants at Quarry Heights without flow-test data. The Supervisor and members expressed strong concern that a fire district would publicly commit in writing not to use available hydrants; the Supervisor plans to meet with the commissioners to understand the dispute. Received; no vote beyond acceptance.

cases.name: Dog Park Expenses — Authorization to Use Fund Balance

timeline.summary: The board approved a memo from the Director of Finance authorizing use of fund balance to pay dog-park expenses, covering fencing, a two-sided dog water fountain, signage, and a water line. The project was built largely in-house by highway and maintenance staff, saving money. Motion carried; grand opening/ribbon-cutting anticipated in weeks.

cases.name: Highway Department Equipment & Vehicle Purchase (Budgeted + CHIPS Funds)

timeline.summary: The board approved a memo from Highway General Foreman Jamie Norris authorizing purchase of equipment and vehicles using budgeted and CHIPS reimbursement funds. Members praised the detailed memo; the Supervisor and a member discussed claiming CHIPS money promptly since the state holds it without interest, and noted long lead times on equipment. Motion carried by voice vote.

cases.name: Highway Facility, Town Hall Project & RFEI — Policy Discussion

timeline.summary: A prolonged, heated discussion branched off the equipment purchase into the town's deferred highway facility and town-hall projects and the town-hall RFEI (request for expressions of interest). One faction pushed to resolve the highway facility quickly, arguing the current yard is a poor gateway to the historic downtown and that a Butler-building band-aid would waste money; another member wanted to keep the highway yard in place and screen it with landscaping and objected to the RFEI's timing, transparency, and an implication that the board wants residential development. The Supervisor forcefully defended the RFEI as merely fact-finding and accused a member's town-wide email of being a political scare tactic. No decision or vote; the matter remains unresolved with a work session planned.

cases.name: Alcohol Permit — State of Play Productions at Whippoorwill Hall

timeline.summary: The board approved an alcohol-permit application for receptions following theatrical performances at Whippoorwill Hall September 4-7, 2025. The Supervisor asked Administrator Kevin to verify the new group's track record in other communities. Motion carried by voice vote.

cases.name: Revised Workplace Violence Policy

timeline.summary: The board initially adopted the revised workplace violence policy with an added 'reasonable person' standard, then rescinded that vote so both this and the sexual-harassment policy could be handled together. It was tabled to a September 10 executive session with labor counsel to produce a clean redraft, targeting a September 24 vote. Councilmember Berra had multiple drafting concerns; other members deferred to labor counsel.

cases.name: Revised Sexual Harassment Policy

timeline.summary: The board debated the revised sexual-harassment policy at length. Councilmember Berra had submitted markups (e.g., substituting 'town board' for 'supervisor,' and adding a right to counsel for the accused), some accepted and some rejected by labor counsel on legal grounds (Civil Service Law §75). Other members (DiGiacinto, Hussain, Milim) were comfortable deferring to labor counsel's expertise but agreed no clean consolidated document existed. On counsel Roland's advice the item was tabled to a September 10 exec session for a clean redraft and a September 24 vote.

cases.name: Consent Judgment & Tax Refund — Stonewall LLC (2019-2023)

timeline.summary: The board received a consent judgment and authorized payment of a tax refund to Stonewall LLC for the 2019-2023 tax years. Motion carried by voice vote. Routine tax-certiorari settlement.

cases.name: Prison Transportation Agreement — Westchester County Dept. of Correction (2025-2026)

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign the 2025-2026 prison transportation agreement with the Westchester County Department of Correction. Town Attorney Roland confirmed it is identical to prior years' agreements. Motion carried.

cases.name: Police Mutual Aid & Rapid Response Plan — Westchester County IMA (2025-2030)

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign an intermunicipal mutual-aid and rapid-response plan for the police departments of Westchester County for the period July 31, 2025 to July 30, 2030. Motion carried by voice vote.

cases.name: First Amendment — Water Contribution & Capital Expenditure Agreement (Toll Brothers / Water District 4)
cases.applicant: Toll Brothers (Airport Campus assignee) / Water District 4

timeline.summary: The board authorized a first amendment to the water contribution and capital expenditure agreement under which Toll Brothers extends water from Westchester Joint Water Works via a new line, tank, and pump house, ultimately allowing Water District 4 to draw on an inexhaustible public supply. Toll's contribution rises to nearly $3M as its share of work escalates to just under $5M while the town's Water District 4 portion drops, netting the town roughly $200,000 positive with a 50/50 cost-share above $5M. Counsel Roland explained the terms; motion carried. The Supervisor hailed the long-sought reliable water source as a major community benefit.

cases.name: Long Pond Park Advisory Committee — Reappointments & Appointment

timeline.summary: The board reappointed Stephen Berman and Susan Scheimer and appointed John Wolf to the Long Pond Park Advisory Committee, each for three-year terms ending August 13, 2028. Supervisor Rende recused himself from the Berman vote (stating he need not file a written explanation under the ethics code). Members praised the appointees' commitment and thanked Kevin Hay for his work preserving Long Pond. Motions carried.

cases.name: Stipulation Agreements with Employees No. 2884 and No. 3244

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign two employee stipulation agreements (Nos. 2884 and 3244). Councilmember Berra had submitted last-minute drafting comments that the Supervisor and DiGiacinto criticized as an unhelpful recurring pattern; other members were comfortable with the agreements as written. Each passed 4-0 with Berra abstaining (citing drafting/exposure concerns, not the substantive terms): DiGiacinto aye, Hussain aye, Milim aye, Rende aye, Berra abstain.

cases.name: Recreation Facilities Update — Turf Field, Pool Upgrades, Clove Road Field

timeline.summary: During administrator and liaison updates the board discussed the turf-field project (fence installed, utility markout done, site survey next), planned pool upgrades (deck removal, releveling/repairing the good-condition stainless gutters, resurfacing, hillside retaining/invasive removal, future locker-room work) to be bid and done over winter, and in-house improvements at Clove Road Field using reused topsoil and better drainage. Members discussed shade structures/pergolas and a possible donation line on pool permits, and noted the county's July 3 fireworks parking may end once the fields are improved. Informational, no vote.

cases.name: Water Conservation Advisory — Summer Drought

timeline.summary: In a liaison update a member urged residents, on well or municipal water, to conserve amid a dry July/August, noting Sal reported some water bills spiking from ~$80 to over $1,000 from lawn watering and pool filling, with usage running 3-4x normal (charges rising steeply with volume). Informational.

cases.name: Closing Memorial — Harry Tompkins

timeline.summary: The Supervisor closed the meeting with a memorial tribute to longtime resident Harry Tompkins, an Eagle Scout who attended American Legion, Memorial Day, and Veterans Day ceremonies, praising his integrity and quiet patriotism. The board offered condolences to his family before adjourning.

cases.name: Extension of RFEI (Request for Expression of Interest) for the Town Hall Project
cases.applicant: Joseph R. Croco, architect (responder requesting extension)

timeline.summary: A late-added agenda item and extensive public-comment topic: an architect responding to the town's RFEI for future municipal facilities requested an extension of the Sept. 22 deadline to Oct. 20. The board consistently agreed earlier that any granted extension would apply to all responders and that no responses would be reviewed until all were received. After lengthy debate about fairness, publicity, and whether granting it could 'taint' or delay the process, the board voted to grant the extension, publicize it widely (website, press, bulletin board, supervisor update), and inform anyone who submits on Sept. 22 that additional time is available. The item became a proxy for a broader fight over how open the RFEI process had been. Passed unanimously.

cases.name: 333 Site / Eminent Domain and Municipal Facilities Direction

timeline.summary: In response to resident questions, the Supervisor explained the town is not currently moving forward on 333 and has not taken the next step on eminent domain, because the community wanted alternatives explored. He recounted how a resident-plus-professional committee was considered but abandoned over cost and composition concerns, leading instead to the free RFEI approach. He stressed that any ultimate direction would go to a voter referendum. No action taken.

cases.name: Daughters of Liberty Legacy Letter — Historic Designation of Two Mount Misery Parcels; Referral to Landmark Preservation Committee
cases.applicant: Cynthia Abbott Coffee, Daughters of Liberty Legacy

timeline.summary: The board received a letter from Cynthia Abbott Coffee requesting historical designation of two town parcels on Mount Misery and referred the matter to the Landmark Preservation Committee (LPC). Members confirmed the LPC referral was included and noted the requester may later make a presentation. Received and referred unanimously.

cases.name: Payment Requisition #1 to Populito Construction — Water District 4 New Well Building Site Work

timeline.summary: The board approved payment requisition #1 to Populito Construction for site work at the Water District 4 new well building; the Supervisor noted the work is progressing well. Discussion with Water/Sewer superintendent 'Sal' pivoted to repurposing a town-owned 3,000-gallon fuel tank (from the old tennis-bubble mechanicals at Community Park) for a water-facility generator rather than leaving it unused. Approved.

cases.name: Receipt of Letter from Patricia Ann Colombo (dated August 10, 2025)

timeline.summary: The board voted to receive a letter from Patricia Ann Colombo dated Aug. 10, 2025, with no substantive discussion. Received.

cases.name: Film Permit — Patch Bay Presence Productions LLC, 15 Middle Patent Road

timeline.summary: The board approved a film permit for Patch Bay Presence Productions LLC to shoot a feature film at 15 Middle Patent Road on Sept. 30–Oct. 1, 2025. Members confirmed the PDF was reviewed and off-site parking arranged; police (Tom McCormick) coordinated staging at the Summit Club as before, with the production described as considerate neighbors previously. Approved.

cases.name: Autism Science Foundation Rides Fair Charity Cycling Event — Town Road & Pool Parking Lot Use
cases.address: Town road and pool parking lot

timeline.summary: The board approved a request from the Autism Science Foundation to use a town road and the pool parking lot for a charity cycling 'rides fair' for autism research on Oct. 4, 2025. The application was amended to bar road spray-paint marking (signs only, to be removed after), and the same group ran it smoothly last year with two applicant-paid police officers. Approved.

cases.name: Authorization to Sign Agreement with ClearGov for New Budget Software

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign an agreement with ClearGov for new budget software, discovered by the Supervisor, Town Administrator Kevin, and Comptroller Abbas at professional conferences. Members praised it as a transparency tool that presents the budget with graphs and pie charts for the public, with a possible capital-planning add-on for five- and ten-year planning. Enthusiastically approved.

cases.name: Stipulation of Agreement with CSEA Unit 2 — Add Water Treatment Operator 2A Position

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign a stipulation of agreement with CSEA Unit 2 adding the Water Treatment Operator 2A position to the collective bargaining agreement. Approved with little discussion.

cases.name: Westchester Joint Water Works — Water District 9 Corey Heights Water Supply Improvements (Water Supply Agreement & Bill of Sale)

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign two agreements for Water District 9 Corey Heights improvements — a water supply agreement and a bill of sale/assumption of obligations transferring the public water mains. Superintendent Sal flagged that Section 5 (page 4), covering NYC DEP per-capita charges and a needed population determination, must be clarified with NYC before it is finalized. The board approved the water supply agreement subject to clarification to the town attorney's satisfaction in consultation with Sal, and separately approved the bill of sale. Two connections are active; the other nine await DEC. Adopted with conditions.

cases.name: Highway Garage Roof Replacement — ELQ Industries via White Plains Job Order Contracting Program
cases.applicant: ELQ Industries (via Gordian / City of White Plains job order contracting)

timeline.summary: The board authorized the Supervisor to sign an agreement with ELQ Industries, via the White Plains job order contracting program, to replace the leaking highway garage roof, to be paid from fund balance since maintenance lines are insufficient. Members lamented the near-$200,000 cost, noting prior estimates of ~$150K and ~$170K in past years were never acted on, on a building 'not even worth saving,' but agreed the holes endanger workers and equipment. The ~10-day job should finish before winter closes the garage. Approved with the fund-balance funding notation.

cases.name: Stipend for Danielle D. Tomas, Senior Office Assistant, Building Department

timeline.summary: The board authorized a stipend for Danielle D. Tomas, senior office assistant in the Building Department, effective Sept. 11, 2025, with members noting she is 'doing the job of two people.' Approved.

cases.name: Resignations/Retirements — Virginia Garcia and Jane Purser (North Castle Public Library)

timeline.summary: The board accepted, with regret and good wishes, a retirement resignation from library assistant Virginia Garcia (effective Sept. 12, 2025) and a resignation from library hourly clerk Jane Purser (effective Aug. 9, 2025). Both accepted.

cases.name: Conference Travel Authorizations — Assessor and Highway Personnel

timeline.summary: The board approved two travel authorizations: Town Assessor Georgeanne Richardson to attend the NYS Assessors Association Fall Conference in Lake George, Oct. 6–9, with a town vehicle; and Highway General Foreman Jamie Norris to attend the League of Municipalities Conference in Atlantic City, Nov. 18–20, with lead mechanic Matthew Harrisch and a town vehicle. Both approved. A consensus agenda was also approved.

cases.name: Proposed Ethics Code Amendments — Agenda Scheduling and Distribution Dispute
cases.applicant: Ethics Board / Town Board Ethics Liaison

timeline.summary: During liaison updates, Councilman Berra (ethics liaison) pressed to distribute special counsel Bob Spolzino's revised ethics-code documents and DiGiacinto's comments and to put receipt of the revised law on the next agenda so a public hearing could be scheduled. The Supervisor said the confidential materials would be distributed the next day but that the item would go on the agenda only after the board deliberates it in executive session, and accused Berra of overreaching as liaison and injecting personal views into the ethics board's work. The exchange escalated into a heated, personal argument involving Rende, Berra, and DiGiacinto over agenda-setting authority (two members may request an item in writing; the Supervisor otherwise sets the agenda), staff use, and prior email blasts. No action taken.

cases.name: Con Edison Proposed 2026 Rate Hikes — Resident Advocacy Appeal

timeline.summary: In her liaison update, Councilwoman DiGiacinto urged residents to email State Senator Shelley Mayer and Assemblyman Chris Burdick (both of whom attended her North White Plains gathering) opposing Con Edison's proposed 2026 delivery rate hikes and to have them forward concerns to the Governor and Public Service Commission. The Supervisor confirmed the town had put out messaging. No action taken.

cases.name: North Castle Public Library Summer Programs Update and Fall Programming

timeline.summary: Councilman Hussain shared a screen presentation of the library's summer statistics — over 30,000 total checkouts including 20,000+ books, 2,800+ audio, 8,000+ ebooks, 310 programs, ~9,000 youth attendees, and ~6,000 books read — and promoted fall programming (meditation, art history, knitting, cooking demos) and the Armonk outdoor art show whose proceeds fund library programs. Celebratory discussion, no action.

cases.name: Supervisor Update — Parks, Turf Field, Dog Park, Water Projects, and Sidewalk Planning

timeline.summary: The Supervisor reported progress across many projects: the turf field, the nearly complete dog park (targeting an early-October ribbon cutting), Clove Road field work, the Quarry Heights playground (with an engineer reviewing drainage from an impervious pad), the swimming pool improvements, School Street and the Water 8-to-4 connection waterline, Quarry Heights water expansion, and cleanup of the Sands Mills historic site. He also asked staff to phase long-deferred sidewalk improvements (a 2005 plan) rather than shelving them as too costly. DiGiacinto pushed to prioritize sidewalks across all three hamlets, noting North White Plains residents walk to the train and stores, not just for exercise. Discussion only.

cases.name: Open Space Committee Work Session — Digital Natural Resources Inventory (NRI) Map
cases.applicant: Open Space Committee (Carrie Kasak, chair) with Westchester County GIS (Anna Geraldo Gomez)

timeline.summary: Open Space Committee chair Carrie Kasak, Town Planner Adam Kaufman, and Westchester County GIS staff presented a web-based Natural Resources Inventory map layering wetlands, forests, slopes, tax parcels, zoning, and other data for every parcel in town, provided free by the county (saving the town thousands). It was described as phase one of a plan leading to a Mianus River Gorge conservation-scoring algorithm and a possible Community Preservation Fund referendum (real-estate transfer tax) via the Trust for Public Land. The tool will be posted publicly and is intended for all boards (Planning, ZBA, Conservation, Town Board). No vote; work session/discussion only.

cases.name: Recognition of Police Department State Re-Accreditation

timeline.summary: Supervisor Rende reported the police department passed its five-year state accreditation review 'with flying colors,' with retired-chief assessors reviewing 112 processes and conducting unannounced ride-alongs and one-on-one interviews. He recognized Chief Simonson, Lt. Huffnagel, Sgts. Joel Thomas and Chris Costa, and the whole department. Board members echoed pride and noted the voluntary process aids public safety and possibly insurance costs. No formal action.

cases.name: Welcome of Fall High-School Interns / Town Internship Program
cases.applicant: Town internship program (spearheaded by Josephine Egan)

timeline.summary: The board welcomed two new high-school interns, Arnhem Das and Jack McNulty, in the town's newly formed rotating internship program (crediting Josephine Egan and the town clerk/administrator offices). Both interns spoke about their interest in local government. Board members encouraged them to ask questions and even criticize the board. No formal action.

cases.name: Clove Field / Community Park Field Improvement Update

timeline.summary: Supervisor Rende updated on the Clove Field project: a next-day meeting with Highway, Parks, and staff (Jamie, Kevin, Matt, Joe Chamele) to set a firm start date, likely early the following week, beginning with drainage rerouting. Topsoil saved from Community Park is stockpiled for relocation to Clove Road, and work is coordinated with contractor Matt DeRosa's turf schedule to finish before winter sod season. Discussion only, including a resident/attendee who asked about timing.

cases.name: Ethics Board Proposed Ethics-Code Amendments (Resident Request for Action)

timeline.summary: During public comment, resident Susan Scheimer (who helped draft the current code) urged the board to act on ethics-code amendments the Ethics Board proposed on January 8, asking that a new public hearing be noticed if that is what it takes to move forward. Supervisor Rende responded that the proposed changes would be discussed with counsel in that evening's executive session and that a new public hearing could likely be set by October 8. No formal action taken in public session.

cases.name: Receipt of Letter from Francesca and Frederick Azada (received Sept 4, 2025)

timeline.summary: The board voted to receive a letter dated/received September 4, 2025 from Francesca and Frederick Azada, submitted as property owners. Brief clarifying discussion on the name/status; motion made, seconded, and carried by voice vote. Routine receipt.

cases.name: Petition Opposing Basketball 'Court' at Quarry Heights Park
cases.address: Quarry Heights Park, North White Plains

timeline.summary: The board formally received a resident petition opposing construction of a basketball court at Quarry Heights Park. Members pushed back on the petition's accuracy, stressing the plan is a small permanent hoop and pad (not a full court, no parking lot), replacing a portable hoop that neighbors the Candreas installed years ago; the chief reported zero complaints about the existing portable hoop. The board voted to receive the petition (motion, second, voice vote) while signaling intent to proceed with the improvement, using pervious asphalt and stockpiled topsoil, and to consider refurbishing the playground in the 2026 budget. Members emphasized keeping kids off the road for safety.

cases.name: Retroactive Special-Event Permit — Spectrum Painting/JB Auto Body Charity Car Show
cases.applicant: Spectrum Painting / JB Auto Body Works

timeline.summary: The board granted retroactive approval of a special-event permit for a charity car show held Sunday, September 28 at 135 Bedford Road, benefiting a women's-cancer foundation. Approved by motion, second, and voice vote, with a request that organizers apply in advance next year. The discussion prompted a plan to revise the local law (with Town Planner Adam Kaufman) to let the board refer routine recurring special-event permits to professional staff rather than hold public hearings, targeting a November meeting.

cases.name: Community Park Artificial-Turf Change Order No. 1 (Shaw Sports Turf) — Sports Lines & Eagle Logo

timeline.summary: The board received a KSCJ Consulting memo and considered Shaw Sports Turf change order no. 1 on the Community Park artificial-turf project, covering added sports-line striping (for two micro soccer fields and a practice football field) and an optional North Castle Eagle logo; a negotiated reduction (3% on striping, 6% with the logo) was secured via Joe Chamele and Matt DeRosa. The board split the vote into two motions. The line package (~$29,677) passed unanimously (5-0). The Eagle logo (~$45,406 before reduction) passed by roll call 3 aye (Milim, Hussain, and presiding Supervisor Rende) to 1 no (DiGiacinto) with 1 abstention (Berra). DiGiacinto criticized the change-order process and the logo cost as cosmetic; supporters argued change orders are normal and the branding adds value.

cases.name: Tie the Town Pink Campaign — Pink Ribbons Benefiting Soul Riders (Barn Hills)

timeline.summary: The board approved the Barn Hills 'Tie the Town Pink' campaign to place pink ribbons around town (Main Street, Town Hall pillars and staircase railings) benefiting Soul Riders, a nonprofit supporting people impacted by cancer. Discussion focused on not rigidly capping the number at nine; the board approved it as proposed, allowing additional reasonable locations. Motion, second, and voice vote.

cases.name: KSCJ Proposal — Water District 4 Extension (Byram Hills HS, Brentwood/Summit) and Supplement to Water District 2 (Windmill)

timeline.summary: The board approved a KSCJ engineering-services proposal to study extending Water District 4 to Byram Hills High School and the proposed Brentwood/Summit community, and to supplement Water District 2 (Windmill) supply, authorizing the supervisor to sign. Water/Sewer Superintendent 'Sal' explained the engineering, elevations, hydraulics, pump-station needs, easements, added fire hydrants, and how selling water to Summit and Windmill creates efficiencies and backup supply while addressing stressed wells and PFAS at the high school. Members noted costs are recovered through district bonds paid by users. Approved by motion, second, and voice vote.

cases.name: Purchase of Radios for Parks & Recreation (Metrocom Wireless, via County Contract)

timeline.summary: The board approved purchasing radios for Parks & Recreation trucks and home bases from Metrocom Wireless through the Westchester County contract. Members noted this puts Highway, Police, and Parks on the same radio system, important for snow emergencies, bad-weather coordination, and school-district bus transportation. Motion, second, and unanimous voice vote.

cases.name: Stipulation Agreement — Town of North Castle, CSEA, and Employee No. 3420

timeline.summary: The board authorized the supervisor to sign a stipulation agreement between the Town of North Castle, the CSEA, and employee number 3420. Approved by motion, second, and voice vote with no substantive discussion in public session.

cases.name: Excelsior Housing Group — Request to Extend RFEI Submission Deadline

timeline.summary: Supervisor Rende raised a same-day letter from Excelsior Housing Group LLC, an interested RFEI respondent, requesting the submission deadline (currently extended to about October 20) be pushed to December 1. Rather than add it as a last-minute item, the board agreed to take it up at the October 8 meeting, with Rende suggesting a possible compromise November date. No action taken; deferred.

cases.name: Local Law to Amend Chapter 127 — Short-Term Rental Regulations

timeline.summary: A work session on a draft local law creating a registration/regulation scheme for short-term rentals, prompted by a severe problem property on Washington Avenue in North White Plains. The board reached rough consensus to keep a primary-residence requirement, retain (over Hussain's and Rende's objection) an owner-must-be-present requirement, reduce the waiting period from four years/two years to two years on the CO and one year of residency, and add quiet-hours provisions. No vote was taken; the planner and building inspector will revise the draft, compile an inventory of existing rentals, and bring it back before scheduling a public hearing.

cases.name: Resolution Supporting Intermunicipal Airport Master Plan Task Force Recommendations
cases.applicant: Airport Master Plan Task Force (rep. Michael Pollock, w/ Larry Ruisi)

timeline.summary: A resolution joining seven municipalities in support of task force recommendations to the county on Westchester County Airport, covering the terminal use agreement (240-passenger/half-hour limit), FBOs, noise, traffic, and environmental concerns. Task force representative Michael Pollock presented and answered extensive questions about the ~80/20 private-vs-commercial traffic split and legal constraints. Adopted 4-1 by roll call, with Milim voting no because he wanted the resolution to push for a larger commercial-carrier share over time. Rende commended Milim for voting his conviction rather than abstaining.

cases.name: Extension of Town Hall Project RFEI Deadline (Excelsior Housing Group request)
cases.address: 45/15 Bedford Road & town hall parcel, Armonk
cases.applicant: Excelsior Housing Group, LLC (via letter from Patrick Normyle)

timeline.summary: Consideration of a letter requesting extension of the deadline to submit an RFEI (Request for Expression of Interest) on the town hall project to Dec 1. After a long and heated debate over the RFEI process itself, the board voted 4-1 to extend the deadline for all respondents to November 10 (aligning with the Nov 12 board meeting). Berra voted no, wanting the process concluded sooner while Milim is still on the board and believing respondents had ample time. The item produced a sharp Rende-DiGiacinto confrontation over whether the RFEI is a political/misleading exercise, with Milim also criticizing DiGiacinto's public messaging as divisive.

cases.name: Sidewalks, Trails & Pedestrian Crosswalk Safety (Parks Board follow-up)
cases.address: Main Street/Rt 128, School Street, Wampus Brook Park (Armonk); Nethermont/Virginia Road (North White Plains)

timeline.summary: During public comment a Parks Board member followed up on ~2.5-year-old survey recommendations for sidewalk/trail extensions in Armonk and an unsafe CVS-area crosswalk on state Route 128. Rende described reviving a shelved comprehensive sidewalk plan and pursuing a staged, grant-and-bond funding approach, noting a prior grant application was denied. The board discussed prioritizing safety segments and coordinating with NYSDOT on the crosswalk and a possible signal; no formal action was taken.

cases.name: Local Law to Amend Chapter 263 Special Events — Remove Public Hearing Requirement

timeline.summary: The board received a proposed local law updating Chapter 263 (special events) to remove the public hearing requirement and scheduled a public hearing on it for October 22, 2025. Received and public hearing set by voice vote.

cases.name: Code of Ethics Amendments — Close Public Hearing & Schedule Work Session

timeline.summary: The board acted on the public hearing opened April 9, 2025 regarding proposed Code of Ethics amendments and set a joint work session with the Ethics Board for the first November meeting (November 12), when the drafting counsel is available. A clean revised draft incorporating minor word changes will be circulated to Ethics Board members by end of week, with the aim of setting a public hearing date after the work session.

cases.name: Revised Town Workplace Violence Policy
