Chief Simonson Chamber honor, cleanup day, Velocity Ride, Troy's Nursery events, Women's History Month tribute.

Advised on hearing procedure and the order of votes (negative declaration before local law), permissive-referendum requirements for land sales, condemnation valuation, and the emergency-access covenant in the Baranovic contract.

Reported on EFC grant-funding meetings for water infrastructure, agreed to arrange proactive soil testing for the turf fields (noting no state-recorded contamination and that arsenic does not migrate from Eagle Ridge), and updated on the north bridge repair and fence ordering.
Director of Planning provided the lead-agency intent notification (Feb 18, 2025) for the water-district action and confirmed County Planning input by email.
Recreation & Parks Superintendent requested authorization to seek pool-concession proposals and was asked to obtain the written eight-year turf-field warranty.

Barbara DiGiacinto recused herself on 23 Bedford Banksville Road (husband part-owner of the mortgage-holding bank); Matt Milim recused on the Lions Club Fol-de-rol (he is club president). cases.name: Special Event Permit — Troy's Nursery Garden Design LLC (Easter + Fall Festivals)
cases.applicant: Troy's Nursery Garden Design LLC (Maria Cece)
cases.summary: A single consolidated special-event permit was sought for an Easter event (April 13, 2025) and two fall festivals (October 5 and 12, 2025), streamlining the applicant's prior year-by-year filings. The board opened the hearing, received PD/fire district/building inspector recommendations, heard the applicant and complimentary board comments, adopted the neg dec and the resolution, and closed the hearing. The board discussed possibly enacting a future local law to allow low-impact, repeat on-premises events with only building-inspector/PD/fire sign-off; special counsel noted that would require a town-code change and could not be done now.
cases.publicComment: Applicant Maria Cece thanked the board for allowing one filing for three events; no resident opposition.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised the event and floated a future local law to streamline low-impact repeat events using other towns (Bedford, Greenwich, Stamford) as a model.
Called it 'always a lovely event, lovely setting' and thanked the applicant.
Said he would support streamlining the process going forward and was 'super excited about the event.'

cases.name: Special Use Permit — 23 Bedford Banksville Road (wood/metal manufacturing)
cases.summary: Following a rezoning to CBB at the prior meeting, the board held a public hearing on a special-use permit to legalize existing specialized wood-product and metal-assemblage manufacturing, with conditions limiting occupancy to 20, keeping storage inside, and requiring proper handling/ventilation of chemicals and fumes. A resident (Jen) questioned why a permit would be granted before the building inspector confirmed safety; counsel and the board explained the operating/building permit review follows the use approval. The board adopted the neg dec and resolution and closed the hearing. A late redline of the conditions circulated the day of the meeting prompted a board member's objection to '11th hour' document changes.
cases.publicComment: Resident 'Jen' voiced strong concern that the site is an eyesore with truck traffic and possible chemicals, and questioned approving the permit before building-inspector clearance; board explained sequencing. Applicant attorney Veneziano described cooperation with the town after prior violations.

memberPositions.evidence: Gave the public a plain-English history of the CBB rezoning and defended the day-of condition changes as previously agreed, saying the applicant had reviewed and agreed to them.
Stressed the area's wetlands and history and that improving the site benefits residents; noted it already looks better.
Said the applicant's client has clearly worked to accommodate the broader town's needs.
A council member objected that board members lacked ample time to review last-minute '11th hour' document changes and urged stopping the practice (speaker not definitively identified).

cases.name: Approval of Town Board Minutes — March 12, 2025
cases.summary: The board approved the minutes of its March 12, 2025 meeting under old business by unanimous voice vote with no discussion.

cases.name: Resolution Opposing Con Ed Proposed Electric & Gas Rate Hikes
cases.summary: The board adopted a multi-page resolution opposing Con Edison's proposed electric and gas rate increases (cited as 11-13%) and supporting State Senator Shelley Mayer's legislation to restrict utility rate hikes, while noting Westchester County's involvement. The supervisor summarized rather than read it in full. Councilwoman DiGiacinto led the effort with the supervisor's confidential secretary Josephine and was thanked for the collaborative work.

memberPositions.evidence: Led drafting with staff, described it as a proud collaborative effort, and thanked Josephine.
Explained the resolution and praised Senator Mayer's legislation and county involvement over merely sending objection emails.

cases.name: Proposed Amendments to Code of Ethics — Receipt & Public Hearing Scheduling
cases.applicant: Board of Ethics (Brett Summers, Sue Scheimer)
cases.summary: The Board of Ethics presented proposed amendments to the Code of Ethics, submitted March 3 in blacklined and local-law form. The Town Board received the proposed amendments and, in a single vote, scheduled a public hearing for April 9, 2025. Members had no questions and thanked the Ethics Board for its work.
cases.publicComment: Ethics Board chair Sue Scheimer and past chair Brett Summers presented; no resident comment.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised the Ethics Board's work, called the changes clear and important, and moved to receive and set the hearing.

cases.name: 2024 Fiscal Year Budget Transfers & Adjustments (Finance Dept. Memo)
cases.summary: The board received a memo from the Director of Finance and authorized budget transfers and adjustments for the 2024 fiscal year. The supervisor characterized it as routine housekeeping to clean up accounting for previously approved expenditures. Adopted by voice vote with no questions.

cases.name: First Amendment to Cider Mill HOA Declaration of Covenants — Consent
cases.summary: The board considered receipt of the First Amendment to the Cider Mill HOA's Declaration of Covenants, Restrictions and Easements and authorization for the supervisor to sign the town's consent, required because the town is a party to the covenant as a condition of the original approval. The supervisor questioned at length why such an internal HOA expense-allocation change comes to the Town Board rather than the Planning Board and raised detailed questions about the allocation percentages, saying he was inclined to abstain. Special counsel Bob Spolzino and Councilman Hussain framed the board's role narrowly as checking for any impact on the town, of which there was none, and the amendment (noted as approved by 80%+ of lot owners) was adopted.
cases.publicComment: No residents appeared to comment despite the item being on the agenda.

memberPositions.evidence: Repeatedly questioned why this internal HOA matter comes to the Town Board and whether it could be delegated to the Planning Board; said he wanted more information and was inclined to abstain but let it proceed.
Argued the board's clear role is to check for negative impact on the broader town; saw none in the document and was 'good to go forward.'

cases.name: Interim MS4 Stormwater Reports (period ending Jan 2, 2025) — Acceptance
cases.summary: The board accepted the interim MS4 stormwater reports for the period ending January 2, 2025, prepared by town engineers KSCJ, and authorized the supervisor to sign. Described as annual housekeeping to promote stormwater safety practices and reduce pollution. Councilwoman DiGiacinto moved it; adopted by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Made the motion to accept the annual stormwater reports.

cases.name: Alcohol Permit & Fee Waiver — Revolutionary War 250 Steering Committee Reception
cases.address: Whippoorwill Hall, North Castle Public Library, Armonk
cases.applicant: North Castle Revolutionary War 250 Steering Committee
cases.summary: The board approved an alcohol permit application from the North Castle Revolutionary War 250 Steering Committee for a reception at Whippoorwill Hall on April 4, 2025 (7 PM), with a waiver of the permit fee. Members thanked committee members, including Ed Woodyard, for their work. Adopted by voice vote.
cases.publicComment: Committee member Ed Woodyard earlier promoted the associated North Castle Revolutionary Town film screenings.

memberPositions.evidence: Thanked the committee for its work on the Revolutionary War 250 commemoration.

cases.name: Town Cleanup Day — Expenditures & Police/Highway Arrangements (April 26, 2025)
cases.summary: The board approved expenditures (minor, historically a few hundred dollars up to a ~$1,000 max) and working arrangements with the police and highway departments for the town-wide cleanup day on Saturday, April 26, 2025 (9 AM-1 PM, rain or shine). The supervisor, liaison to the sustainability committee, described the resident-driven event and safety emphasis and credited volunteers. Councilman Milim thanked the board for reviving the event.

memberPositions.evidence: As sustainability committee liaison, championed the revived cleanup day and credited resident volunteers.
Thanked the supervisor for reviving the event, saying he had done it with his son and it was 'really great.'

cases.name: Armonk Lions Club Fol-de-rol at Wampus Brook Park (June 5-8, 2025)
cases.summary: The board approved the Armonk Lions Club's request to hold the Fol-de-rol at Wampus Brook Park June 5-8, 2025. Councilman Milim recused himself as Lions Club president (deeming himself an interested officer under the ethics code) but, after discussion, spoke about the event in his individual capacity; the supervisor and Ethics Board chair questioned whether recusal was even required. Members praised Milim's revitalization of the club and noted the Lions' $20,000 donation to the Wampus North Bridge repair and other charitable giving. Adopted by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Recused as club president but spoke personally about how the Fol-de-rol drew him to town and detailed the club's charitable donations; clearly enthusiastic.
Argued Milim likely did not need to recuse (no financial interest as a volunteer officer) and praised his revival of the club.

cases.name: License Agreement — Mount Pleasant PD Communication Equipment on Custis Water Tower
cases.summary: The board approved a license agreement letting the Mount Pleasant Police Department install communication equipment on the Custis water tower to cover dead spots, and authorized the supervisor to sign. In a reciprocal arrangement Mount Pleasant PD will install North Castle's new two-way communication equipment at no cost, and pays the power costs; a formal license was needed due to an access easement. Adopted by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Explained the mutually beneficial partnership with Mount Pleasant PD and recommended approval.

cases.name: Two-Way Radio Communications Satellite Receiver System — Metrocom Wireless Proposal
cases.applicant: Police Chief Pete Simonson / Metrocom Wireless Inc.
cases.summary: At the police chief's request, the board approved funding a two-way radio communications satellite receiver system and a Metrocom Wireless Inc. proposal of roughly $14,000 to replace older equipment and eliminate communication dead spots. The expandable system will also serve highway, water and sewer and enable cross-department coordination in emergencies. Adopted by voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Explained the upgrade fixes dead spots and is expandable at no install cost thanks to Mount Pleasant PD.
Highlighted that highway, water and sewer will also use the system to coordinate during snowstorms and emergencies.

cases.name: IBM Community Park Artificial Turf Field Improvements (~$4.1M)
cases.applicant: Town of North Castle (Derosa Sports Construction via Sourcewell co-op)
cases.summary: The board received the Westchester County DPW and NYS DEC lead-agency circulation responses, adopted a negative declaration, and approved the roughly $4.1 million agreement (via Sourcewell cooperative purchasing with Derosa Sports Construction) for artificial turf fields at IBM 1 and 2, plus a Hydro Environmental Solutions proposal for soil-fill testing. Councilman Milim championed the project with survey and park-and-rec data showing turf as the top-requested capital project; the supervisor and Councilman Hussain strongly supported paying from the ~$25M fund balance rather than bonding. Councilwoman DiGiacinto urged bonding instead and raised concerns about not doing soil testing first given possible contamination and about future capital needs (town hall, pool, water lines). Numerous residents spoke in strong support, and all items were adopted by voice vote.
cases.publicComment: Multiple residents (including former Park & Rec advisory board member Jen Clark, now Armonk Soccer Club regional commissioner) spoke strongly in favor, stressing the fields' poor condition, benefit to children, and urgency to vote; several urged testing all town fields for contamination.

memberPositions.evidence: Led the multi-year effort, presented survey data ranking turf the #1 requested project, explained lifecycle economics (~$4.1M lasting 40-50 yrs with ~$850K resurfacing), and argued fund balance is the appropriate source, not bonding.
Called it a compelling quality-of-life investment, criticized 'paralysis through analysis' and repeated delay, and argued doing the project actually addresses (encapsulates) any soil concern.
Said fund balance is a proper use and soil testing shouldn't be a dependency; argued contamination, if found, makes the turf project more compelling since excavation costs would be shared.

Supported the need but urged bonding rather than fund balance given upcoming big expenses, regretted that soil testing wasn't done first, and suggested per-child user 'head fees' to offset maintenance.

cases.name: Personnel Actions — Appointment, Salary Adjustments, Terminal Leave, Training
cases.summary: The board approved a slate of personnel items by successive voice votes: probationary appointment of Thomas Farrington as skilled laborer in Water & Sewer (eff. March 31, 2025); salary adjustments for Library Director Kathryn Feely and Assistant Library Director Angela Cook (eff. Jan 1, 2025); terminal leave payments for William Gallagher (Water & Sewer) and Angel Morales (Police); and authorization for Patrick Ritchie to attend a NYS tax receivers/collectors training in Lake George (June 8-11, 2025). The consensus agenda was then approved.

themes.note: Dominated by the IBM Community Park turf field approval plus cleanup day and Fol-de-rol.
Central to the fund-balance-vs-bonding debate on turf; also budget transfers and the Con Ed rate resolution.
23 Bedford Banksville special-use permit and the Cider Mill HOA covenant amendment.
Special-event permit, Rev War 250 reception, cleanup day, and Fol-de-rol all favorably received.
Mount Pleasant PD tower license and the Metrocom two-way radio upgrade.
Debate over last-minute document changes, the board's role in HOA covenants, and streamlining event permits.
Soil-contamination concern at IBM fields, MS4 stormwater reports, and cleanup day.
Con Ed rate-hike resolution, Senator Mayer legislation, and Mount Pleasant PD agreement.
Routine appointment, salary, terminal-leave, and training approvals.

staffInput.summary: Delivered community announcements, read the affidavits of posting/publication and application documents for both public hearings, and circulated the redlined 23 Bedford conditions the day of the meeting.

As special counsel, advised that streamlining event permits would require a town-code change, and explained (per Roland) that the town is a party to HOA covenants as a permit condition so the board's role is limited to checking for town impact.
Confirmed the MS4 stormwater reports were routine annual housekeeping and supported the police/communications upgrades.
Submitted the memo underlying the 2024 budget transfers and adjustments (housekeeping to reconcile approved expenditures).
Town Planner (attended remotely); drafted the 23 Bedford special-permit resolution and conditions that the board and applicant praised.

meetings.attributionNote: Speakers were largely identifiable by role and context: Supervisor Rende presided remotely by Zoom ('Joe Rendez joining us by zoom'); Milim (turf champion, Lions Club president recusal) and DiGiacinto (Con Ed resolution, turf bonding concern, recusal on 23 Bedford) were clearly identified; Hussain identified via 'Saleem/Salim/Celine' manglings. Jose Berra is present (Deputy Supervisor) but had little distinctive substantive dialogue; the '11th hour' document-change objection during the 23 Bedford hearing was made by a non-presiding council member whose identity is uncertain (tentatively Berra, low confidence). Barbara DiGiacinto recused on 23 Bedford Banksville Rd; Matt Milim recused on the Lions Club Fol-de-rol. Staff names normalized (DiGiacinto ASR 'digisono'; Comptroller 'Abbasura' = Abbas). Sonny Vitaj not applicable (2026 only).

meetings.meetingSummary: The Town Board opened with a lengthy work session on modernizing the town sign law, focusing on how to regulate temporary and political signs in a content-neutral, First Amendment-compliant way. The centerpiece of the regular meeting was a contentious public hearing on proposed Code of Ethics amendments (campaign-contribution recusal, a ban on electeds serving as party officers, and applicant disclosure), which drew sharp disagreement and was adjourned and referred to legal counsel. The board also awarded a water district bid, approved several water/sewer engineering proposals, licenses and payment requisitions, authorized special counsel for a Con Edison rate case, adopted a pedestrian-improvement resolution, and accepted a Planning Board member's resignation amid a heated exchange over the IBM turf-field project.
meetings.durationNote: Full board present (Rende, DiGiacinto, Hussain, Milim, Berra); meeting ran past 12:30 a.m. Opened 5:30 p.m. with an executive session on personnel and real estate.

cases.name: Sign Law Modernization — Work Session
cases.summary: A work session (no vote) on updating the town's sign law to remove content-based restrictions and comply with the Supreme Court's Reed decision, resurrected after a year on the back burner. Debate centered on temporary and political signs: whether to require registration, how many temporary signs to allow per property, whether to permit longer display for special-event/250th banners, and whether designated sign areas or private-property placement is better. No decision was made; members agreed to submit written comments to Adam Kaufman (copying the full board and counsel) by roughly end of month, with another work session to follow.
cases.publicComment: Resident Sue Scheimer recalled a past inter-party agreement to forgo political signs and urged the parties to revert to that practice.

memberPositions.evidence: Wanted special-event/250th banners allowed longer (via variance or board approval) but opposed registering temporary signs as a burden on the building department; favored an organization contact-person model so town resources aren't spent removing signs.
Said political signage is a nuisance and not positive; would ideally ban temporary signs; pushed for one temporary sign per property with registration and a property-owner permission attestation.
Favored limiting to two or three signs (one is too restrictive), warned against hurting community events (art show, 5Ks, festivals), and liked the organization contact-person registry.
Probed whether the town could offer approved temporary-sign designs and whether signs could be restricted; generally open to registration with two to three signs allowed.
Had suggested trimming the introductory findings/preamble as longer than necessary and wanted the draft law simplified.

cases.name: Public Hearing — Code of Ethics Amendments
cases.summary: Public hearing on Board of Ethics-recommended amendments: barring a town board member/candidate from voting on matters involving anyone who contributed over $500 in the aggregate (effective no earlier than Jan 1, 2026), an apportionment rule for committee contributions, a failure-to-file-disclosure violation, applicant disclosure for real-property applications (27.6F), a bar on land-use committee members representing third parties (27.10), and a prohibition on electeds/department heads serving as political party officers (27.22-C). Supervisor Rende voiced strong opposition to the party-officer ban and mandatory contribution-based recusal as a First Amendment overreach, while other members largely supported the package with reservations. After extensive debate the board adjourned the public hearing (no adoption) and, by roll-call vote, referred both the Board of Ethics recommendations and Councilman Berra's redline changes to legal counsel for a written opinion, targeting reopening by roughly June 11.
cases.publicComment: Board of Ethics members (e.g., Brett Summers and a member citing Caperton v. Massey) presented and defended the amendments, arguing the recusal rule is constitutional and aimed at curbing developer influence; exchanges were pointed.

memberPositions.evidence: Called several changes a 'travesty' and overreach, argued contribution limits and the party-officer ban raise First Amendment problems and could invite costly litigation, favored preserving disclosure over barring votes, and pushed to refer everything to counsel; supported the 27.10 third-party-representation ban and failure-to-file clause.

Objected to the repeated 'developers' framing as unfair to the board, raised concern about ethics-board liaison interference, questioned why planning-board applicants must disclose town-board contributions, and flagged an errant town-attorney reference in 27.22-C.

Supported most provisions including the $500 recusal 'better than what we have,' but opposed the 27.22 political-party restriction as reaching into personal capacity and warned the $500 rule could be gamed by candidate slates.
Favored more guardrails to build community trust, argued ethics needs explicit rules not just an inner compass, but wanted to think more about the 27.22 party-officer limitation.
Participated in the ethics-board deliberations and submitted redline changes (including extending the bar to unsuccessful candidates) that were referred to counsel alongside the main package.

cases.name: Licensing Agreement Request — Main Street Property (Michael)
cases.summary: An applicant appeared to request a license agreement from the town relating to on-street parking spaces that cross a property line, referred to the board by the Town Planner. Because no license agreement had been drafted or submitted, the board tabled the matter, directing the applicant's attorney to prepare and submit the agreement for review and to verify with the Planning Department whether any existing variance runs with the property. Motion to table passed.

memberPositions.evidence: Suggested tabling until the license agreement is drafted and the variance status is verified with planning.

cases.name: Approval of Town Board Minutes — March 26, 2025
cases.summary: The board approved the minutes of the March 26, 2025 town board meeting. Routine consent item, motion carried.

cases.name: Landmark Designation of the Eagle (Routes 128 & 22)
cases.summary: The board received the Landmark Preservation Committee's recommendation to landmark the Eagle monument and surrounding streetscape at Routes 128 and 22 and scheduled a public hearing for May 14, 2025. Questions remain about whether to include the land (as opposed to just the monument), plus boundary/deed issues that may require a survey. The board voted to receive the recommendation (to be supplemented) and set the hearing date.

memberPositions.evidence: Willing to keep the May 14 hearing date while noting a marked survey may be needed to resolve boundary questions.
As a committee member, described wanting a protective streetscape around the eagle; also reported a replacement plaque was made and will be mounted.

cases.name: Bid Award — Water District #4 (School Street) Extension
cases.summary: The board awarded the construction bid for the Water District No. 4 School Street extension to Southern Industries Corp., following evaluation of 11 bids and a recommendation from the engineer's office. Members emphasized holding a pre-construction meeting as was successfully done on the prior (Casale) project. Motion carried.

memberPositions.evidence: Stressed a pre-construction meeting for coordination, citing the smooth prior project.

cases.name: Water District #4 Rehabilitation (IBM/Northwell Well)
cases.summary: The board approved a series of actions for rehabilitating the IBM (Northwell) well in Water District No. 4: receiving the superintendent's memo, authorizing going to bid, approving an RFP for a replacement well pump, and approving WSP Engineering's proposal for project oversight. Supervisor Rende recused himself on this item due to its relation to the IBM community park. All motions carried.

memberPositions.evidence: Recused himself from this item because it relates to the IBM community park.

cases.name: AI Engineering Proposal — Quarry Heights Water District #9 Extension (Map, Plan & Report)
cases.summary: The board approved AI Engineering's proposal for the required map, plan and report to extend Water District No. 9 (Quarry Heights), the first legal step toward bringing water service to remaining area residents. The firm, already familiar with the terrain from prior feasibility and sewer work, will follow with a separate design/construction-management proposal; the town is also researching grant funding. A member confirmed any out-of-scope work would require board approval before payment. Motion carried.

memberPositions.evidence: Questioned the reimbursable/sub-consultant expense language, confirming out-of-scope work must come back for approval before payment.

cases.name: Payment Requisition #1 — Tony Casale Inc. (Kent Place / Verizon Parking Improvements)
cases.summary: The board approved payment requisition No. 1 to Tony Casale Incorporated for the Kent Place Verizon parking plan improvements. Members noted the work is nearly finished and agreed it is time to start the conversation on the remainder of the parking lot/district. Motion carried.

cases.name: Payment Requisition — J.T. Oranzio (Wampus Brook Park North Bridge)
cases.summary: The board approved a payment requisition to J.T. Oranzio for the Wampus Brook Park North Bridge replacement, with members praising the finished work. The board thanked the Lions Club, which committed $20,000 from folder-roll fundraising toward the project. Motion carried.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised the completed bridge work.

cases.name: Alcohol Permit — Katona Classic Stage (Whippoorwill Hall)
cases.address: Whippoorwill Hall, North Castle Public Library, Armonk
cases.summary: The board approved an alcohol permit application from Katona Classic Stage for theatrical performances at Whippoorwill Hall, April 24 to May 4, 2025. Routine motion carried.

cases.name: Liquor License — L&M Restaurant Inc., 405 Main Street
cases.summary: The board received a new liquor license application from L&M Restaurant Inc. at 405 Main Street and waived the 30-day notice. Councilwoman DiGiacinto recused herself because the property is owned by the DiGiacinto family, citing it as an example of self-checking for ethics conflicts. Motion carried.

memberPositions.evidence: Recused herself because 405 Main Street is owned by the DiGiacinto family, though she derives no benefit.

cases.name: Liquor License — Massarella Italian Steakhouse, 111 Bedford Road
cases.summary: The board received a new liquor license application from Nezeraj Incorporated for Massarella Italian Steakhouse at 111 Bedford Road and waived the 30-day notice. Motion carried.

cases.name: Library RFP — Branding, Website Redesign & Event Calendar
cases.applicant: North Castle Public Library (Director Katherine Feeley)
cases.summary: The board authorized the library director to issue an RFP for branding, website redesign and an event calendar system. Councilwoman DiGiacinto objected that the project was not in the 2025 budget and that unresolved safety issues (electrical panel, water/sewer, teen-room waterproofing) should take priority; staff reported those items are being addressed. The board approved authorizing the RFP on condition that the final RFP be reviewed through the town administrator's office and that any resulting bid/award return to the board for approval. Motion carried.

memberPositions.evidence: Objected that it was not budgeted and that library safety issues (electrical, water/sewer, teen-room waterproofing) should be addressed first; called the request inappropriate at this time.
As library liaison, offered to convey the budget/prioritization concerns and asked the library to be clear on needs and resident impact.
Supported issuing the RFP but conditioned it on final review through the town administrator's office before it goes out.

cases.name: Resolution Supporting Pedestrian Improvements Throughout the Town
cases.applicant: North Castle Parks & Recreation Advisory Board (Carl Hendricks)
cases.summary: The board received a letter from the Parks & Recreation Advisory Board requesting sidewalks connecting downtown Armonk to Lombardy Park/the town pool, and adopted a broader resolution committing to pursue pedestrian improvements throughout all three hamlets in the most cost-effective way. Councilwoman DiGiacinto pressed that North White Plains has long sought Route 22 and Virginia Road sidewalks and urged a multi-year capital-priority approach. Motion carried.

memberPositions.evidence: Supported pedestrian access but questioned the pool-path priority, noting North White Plains' long-standing Route 22/Virginia Road requests and the need to prioritize big-ticket capital items.
Framed the resolution as a commitment to keep pedestrian access a priority across all hamlets and pursue it in sections cost-effectively.

cases.name: Special Counsel — Dichter Law for Con Edison Rate Case
cases.applicant: Joel R. Dichter / Dichter Law LLC
cases.summary: The board authorized hiring Joel R. Dichter of Dichter Law LLC as special counsel to represent North Castle, alongside other Westchester municipalities, in the Consolidated Edison electric and gas rate case before the Public Service Commission. With about 39 municipalities joining, the per-town cost dropped from an estimated $5,000 to roughly $2,700. Members discussed potential conflicts if the firm represented other counties but were satisfied it would not. Motion carried.

memberPositions.evidence: Called it a worthwhile endeavor against 'horrible' rate increases, noting most of the increase is on delivery.
Drafted the supporting resolution and probed potential conflict-of-interest concerns.

cases.name: Westchester County Municipal Police Mobile Radio Program Agreement
cases.summary: The board approved participation in the Westchester County Municipal Police Department's mobile radio program and authorized the supervisor to sign the agreement. Members noted police staff (Tom McCormick and Pete Simonson) had vetted and were satisfied with the terms. Motion carried.

cases.name: Metropolitan Regional Radio System (MRRS) Access Agreement with MTA Police
cases.summary: The board approved the Metropolitan Regional Radio System (MRRS) systems access agreement with the MTA Police Department and authorized the supervisor to sign. Routine motion carried.

cases.name: License Agreement — Fisher Lane Meter Parking Lot (Westchester County)
cases.summary: The board approved the license agreement with Westchester County for the Fisher Lane meter parking lot for the period April 1, 2025 through March 31, 2026, and authorized the supervisor to sign. Motion carried.

cases.name: Resignation — Jim Jensen, Planning Board
cases.summary: The board received the resignation of Planning Board member Jim Jensen, effective March 27, 2025, after 11 years of service. DiGiacinto read Jensen's stated reason — that the town bypassed site-plan review for the IBM community park (turf-field) project, which he viewed as an ethical issue — triggering a heated exchange over whether the project was handled properly. Rende and Milim defended the process (engineer and DEC review, no shortcuts) and argued the Planning Board review was not required, while DiGiacinto maintained a public hearing/planning review should have occurred; Berra, the Planning/Conservation liaison, had not objected to skipping review. The board voted to accept the resignation with thanks. Motion carried.

memberPositions.evidence: Sympathetic to Jensen's concern, stressed there was no public hearing and that she had recommended Planning/Conservation Board review of the turf-field project.
Defended the turf-field process as fully reviewed by the engineer and DEC with no corners cut; regretted the resignation but disputed any 'bypass' impropriety.
Argued against unnecessary red tape and sending projects to extra boards when already properly reviewed; called delay the root of residents' frustration with government.
As Planning/Conservation Board liaison, did not think sending the project to those boards was necessary and did not object at the time.

cases.name: Public Comment — Meeting Participation Rules, 250th Anniversary & Town Cleanup
cases.summary: During public comment and community announcements, residents raised several matters. Ed Loberman urged the board to restore the public speaking time limit from three minutes to five and to allow public comment on all agenda items in person (not just via Zoom or at public hearings). Ed Woodyard updated on the 250th-anniversary documentary screenings and historic-site preservation efforts (Sands Mill, Miller Hill), prompting Rende to float purchasing a replica cannon for the Miller Hill battlefield. The town-wide cleanup (April 26, 9 a.m.–1 p.m.) was promoted by sustainability liaison Jose Berra. No formal action taken.
cases.publicComment: Ed Loberman (positive/constructive) advocated a five-minute speaking limit and broader in-person comment rights; Ed Woodyard and Sue Scheimer spoke warmly about the 250th film, historic preservation, and the cleanup.

memberPositions.evidence: As sustainability liaison, promoted the April 26 town-wide cleanup, described logistics (orange bags, vests, grabbers) and encouraged family participation.
Enthused about the 250th documentary and historic sites, proposing research toward buying a replica cannon for the Miller Hill battlefield.

themes.note: Dominated by the ethics-code public hearing and disputes over process, disclosure, liaison roles and public participation.
First Amendment and litigation-risk concerns pervaded the sign law and ethics debates; special counsel retained for the Con Ed rate case.
Sign law modernization, ethics disclosure for real-property applicants, and the turf-field/Planning Board review dispute.
Several water-district actions advanced: District 4 bid award, IBM-well rehab, and Quarry Heights District 9 extension.
Bridge, parking, sidewalk and water projects, plus calls to prioritize big-ticket capital needs like town hall and highway yard.
Contentious acceptance of Planning Board member Jim Jensen's resignation.
Police radio agreements, county parking-lot license, and multi-town Con Ed rate-case coalition.
250th anniversary film, historic-site preservation, landmark eagle, and town cleanup.
Two liquor licenses and an alcohol permit approved; one licensing request tabled.
Concerns about unbudgeted library RFP spending and capital prioritization.

staffInput.summary: Town Planner presented the sign-law overview and Reed-compliance rationale, walked through draft provisions, and (referenced) submitted grant applications for sidewalks.
Sitting Town Attorney advised on legal/constitutional questions in the sign and ethics matters, the licensing agreement process, landmark boundary/deed issues, and the ethics referral to counsel.
Read correspondence and public hearing notices, handled public-comment sign-ups, provided cleanup and deed information, and noted state filing timelines for the ethics local law.
Advised on the library RFP framework and building repairs, reported on radio agreements and grant research, and noted recreation/water-sewer hiring.
Water/Sewer superintendent presented and recommended action on the District 4 bid award, IBM-well rehabilitation steps, and the Quarry Heights District 9 extension.

meetings.attributionNote: Full board present (Rende, DiGiacinto, Hussain, Milim, Berra); no Vitaj (2026 only). The unlabeled ASR made speaker identification hard on the long sign-law and ethics segments; the presiding/supervisor voice was mapped to Rende and roll-call/named exchanges used to attribute Milim, DiGiacinto, Hussain and Berra. Board of Ethics presenters (e.g., Brett Summers, Sue) are a town committee, treated as public/committee input, not board members. Some names garbled (DiGiacinto as 'Digacino/Dejacinto', Berra as 'Barra/Barros/Bara', Kaufman references). Lower-confidence attributions flagged where the speaker could not be pinned down.

meetings.meetingSummary: The North Castle Town Board reconvened from executive session and handled a full consent-heavy agenda plus several substantive items. It reopened and immediately adjourned (to an undetermined date) the public hearing on the eminent-domain acquisition of 333 Main Street, adopted a home-rule hotel-occupancy-tax resolution, approved a series of subdivision, wetland-mitigation and stormwater bonds and easements, authorized vehicle purchases and highway/pool/ballfield contracts, and made personnel and board appointments. The two most debated items were a $161,000 (~60%) increase to the EDR wastewater-treatment-plant engineering agreement (adopted by roll call over Councilman Berra's request for a cost breakdown) and a fee-waiver request from Mianus River Gorge (tabled pending a townwide nonprofit fee-waiver policy). The board also declined a Rochambeau 'Victory Towns' membership in favor of funding its own historical marker.
meetings.durationNote: Meeting opened at 5:30 p.m. and recessed to executive session (boards/committees, personnel, real estate); reconvened in open session with a quorum. All five members present (Rende, DiGiacinto, Hussain, Milim, Berra); no absences noted.

cases.name: Public Hearing — Acquisition of 333 Main Street via Eminent Domain
cases.summary: The board reconvened the public hearing to consider acquiring 333 Main Street under the Eminent Domain Procedure Law. As noticed, the hearing was opened and immediately adjourned to an undetermined future date because the board is still gathering information. Resident Andrew Lester spoke against the acquisition, calling the property undesirable and urging a holistic, process-driven review before proceeding.
cases.publicComment: Andrew Lester (68 Byron Ridge Road) opposed the acquisition, arguing the property is undesirable, that repurposing the existing footprint would be cheaper, and that the board should scrutinize who has a vested interest before acting; skeptical/cautionary tone.

memberPositions.evidence: Explained the hearing would open and be adjourned while the board continues gathering information before setting a continuation date.

cases.name: Invasive Vine Mitigation Volunteer Program
cases.summary: During public comment, resident Doug Mancinelli reported on the volunteer invasive-vine mitigation program launched three months ago, with eight successful events and 20+ volunteers at sites including the Erico property, Smith's Tavern and Sands Mill. He invited residents to upcoming events at the town pool. The board was enthusiastic; the Supervisor praised the effort and asked for a volunteer list so the town could send thank-you letters.
cases.publicComment: Doug Mancinelli presented enthusiastically and thanked the town (and Jose Berra and staff) for support; several board members complimented the program.

memberPositions.evidence: Called it a fantastic, long-overdue program and requested a volunteer list so the board could send letters of appreciation.

cases.name: Home Rule Request to Extend Hotel Occupancy Tax Legislation
cases.summary: The board adopted a resolution making a home-rule request to the NYS Senate and Assembly to extend the hotel occupancy tax enabling legislation. Although the town currently has no hotel, keeping the legislation in place preserves the ability to collect the tax if a hotel is built in the future; proceeds are stipulated for road repair and maintenance. Adopted on a voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Explained the value of keeping the legislation in place so hotel-tax revenue (earmarked for roads) could be collected in the future.

cases.name: Whale Ass Way Subdivision — Inspection Fee, Bonds and Townsend Burial Ground Easements
cases.summary: The board acted on several Whale Ass Way items: accepting a KSCJ recommendation on the subdivision inspection fee and a stormwater performance bond, receiving a Singleton Davis & Singleton letter, and approving a declaration of easements/maintenance agreement for access to the Townsend burial ground plus the stormwater facilities construction/maintenance agreement, authorizing the Supervisor to sign (including form TP-584). Councilman Berra raised detailed questions about public access to the historic cemetery, insolvency notice provisions, and a rubber-stamp change clause. The declaration was adopted with a condition correcting the performance-guarantee amount to $230,298.48. All items passed on voice votes.

memberPositions.evidence: Pressed on cemetery access language, insolvency-notice responsibility, and whether change-approval clauses should be narrowed; ultimately supported passage and secured the corrected bond amount and limited historical access for the 250th anniversary.
Moved the items forward, folded Berra's bond-amount correction into the motion, and kept the votes on track.

cases.name: Cassone Special Use Permit Amendment — Private Equestrian Use
cases.address: 22 Cowdery Drive and 50 Round Hill Road, Armonk, NY
cases.summary: The board received a special-use-permit application from Mary Lou Cassone to amend a 1992 permit recognizing continued private equestrian use alongside the principal dwelling, and scheduled a public hearing for May 14, 2025. On the Town Attorney's advice, it also voted to refer the matter to the North Castle and Westchester County planning boards and to declare the Town Board lead agency for SEQRA. Passed on voice votes.

memberPositions.evidence: Moved to schedule the hearing and adopted the attorney-recommended referral and lead-agency motions.

cases.name: Mianus River Gorge — Planning Board Fee Waiver Request
cases.summary: The nonprofit Mianus River Gorge requested a waiver/reduction of the ~$300 planning board filing fees (not the professional escrow) for a site-plan application to renovate office space. The board debated at length whether to grant it: the Supervisor and Councilwoman DiGiacinto objected to acting without a townwide policy and criteria for nonprofit fee waivers, while another member argued fairness favored granting a reduction for a worthy nonprofit. The board voted to table the item and asked Town Planner Adam Kaufman (via the Administrator) to draft a fee-waiver policy for board review.

memberPositions.evidence: Said it was 'not really a precedent I'm comfortable with or supportive of at this time' and pushed for a policy with criteria before waiving any fees.
Agreed the board should adopt a policy with criteria before waiving fees rather than deciding case-by-case on the floor.

Framed the decision around fairness and consistency, asked how often waivers had been requested, and said he'd be open to a reduction for a nonprofit or hardship while also supporting a consistent process.

cases.name: Water/Sewer Department Memo on Fire District Agreements — Referral to Town Attorney
cases.summary: The board received a memo dated April 15, 2025 from the water/sewer department director regarding fire district agreements and referred the matter to the Town Attorney. Adopted on a voice vote with no substantive debate.

cases.name: Purchase of F-150 and F-250 Pickup Trucks for Water & Sewer Department
cases.summary: The board approved purchasing a new Ford F-150 and F-250 for the water and sewer department through the Sourcewell cooperative contract, paid from the 2025 operating budget. The Supervisor confirmed with Sal that the vehicles were budgeted, came in under budget by over $2,000, and replace vehicles due for replacement. Adopted on a voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Confirmed the trucks were budgeted, came in under budget, and replaced vehicles needing replacement before moving approval.

cases.name: Purchase of F-350 Pickup Truck for Parks Department
cases.applicant: Parks Department (National Auto Fleet Group / Sourcewell)
cases.summary: The board approved purchasing a Ford F-350 for the parks department from the National Auto Fleet Group through the Sourcewell contract, funded by the 2025 operating budget, at roughly a 3.5% discount. The Administrator confirmed it replaces a vehicle coming out of service. Adopted on a voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Noted the truck replaces one leaving service and secured about a 3.5% discount before approval.

cases.name: Wetland Mitigation Performance/Monitoring Bonds — Bella, Kamar and Rogel Residences
cases.address: 3 Seymour Place West; 75 Hickory Kingdom Road; 18 Caroline Place
cases.summary: On KSCJ Consulting recommendations, the board established wetland mitigation bonds for three residential projects: a performance bond plus five-year monitoring/maintenance bond for the Bella residence (3 Seymour Place West), the same for the Kamar residence (75 Hickory Kingdom Road), and a five-year monitoring/maintenance bond for the Rogel residence (18 Caroline Place). Each item passed on a routine voice vote.

cases.name: Kent Place / Verizon Parking Lot Improvements — Payment Requisition No. 4 (Tony Casal Inc.)
cases.address: Kent Place / Verizon parking lot, Armonk
cases.summary: On a KSCJ recommendation, the board approved payment requisition No. 4 to Tony Casal Inc. for the Kent Place/Verizon parking lot improvements. Members reported the final asphalt layer was laid that day, with only lighting and some fencing remaining, and praised the contractor and town staff (Kevin, Jamie, Joe Chimelli of Kellard). The Supervisor also flagged advancing the broader parking-district plan via a public informational work session. Adopted on a voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised the contractor and staff for a great job, noted the final asphalt was laid, and urged putting the parking-district plan on the 'front burner.'

cases.name: Jewish Board of Family and Children Services — Cycle of Support Cycling Event
cases.applicant: Jewish Board of Family and Children Services
cases.summary: The board approved a request from the Jewish Board of Family and Children Services to use town roads and parks for a 'Cycle of Support' cycling event on Sunday, September 14. Per an uploaded note from Police Lieutenant McCormick, roughly five police officers (subject to adjustment) will provide presence, paid for by the applicant. Adopted on a voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Confirmed PD sign-off and that the applicant pays for the required police presence before approval.

cases.name: Washington-Rochambeau Revolutionary Route (W3R-US) 'Victory Towns' Membership
cases.summary: The board considered joining the W3R-US 'Victory Towns' membership program at either a $2,200 or $4,500 level; resident Ed Woodyard urged the higher tier so the Supervisor could attend a Philadelphia event. The Supervisor and Councilwoman DiGiacinto viewed the membership as essentially a donation with little tangible benefit, preferring instead to fund the town's own historical marker/plaque (e.g., at Sands Mill) using suggested commemorative language. The item was tabled.
cases.publicComment: Ed Woodyard advocated for the more expensive leadership-tier membership, emphasizing North Castle's Revolutionary War significance.

memberPositions.evidence: Called it 'a bit of a money grab' and said $4,500 could buy many signs; preferred investing in the town's own marker.
Said 'for $2,200 I'm not seeing it,' viewed the membership as a donation, and favored a lasting town-created plaque instead.

cases.name: EDR Contract Amendment — Sewer District No. 2 Wastewater Treatment Plant Upgrade
cases.address: Sewer District No. 2 Wastewater Treatment Plant
cases.summary: The board considered an amendment to EDR's June 2020 contract for the Sewer District No. 2 wastewater plant upgrade, adding roughly $161,000 (~60%) to accommodate Westchester County Health Department backwash-filtration requirements that forced a redesign (additional pumping station, revised drawings) over five years. Superintendent Sal gave a detailed presentation explaining the non-mandated nitrogen-reduction enhancement and why costs rose. Councilman Berra pressed for a breakdown showing the increase was 'fair and equitable,' while the Supervisor expressed full confidence in Sal and the rest of the board favored proceeding. The amendment was adopted by roll call, with EDR to still provide a cost breakdown for the file.

memberPositions.evidence: Flagged the ~60% ($161,000) increase on what was meant to be a fixed-cost contract and asked for a detailed breakdown proving the amount was fair and equitable, without wanting to hold up the vote.
Expressed 'utmost faith' in Sal, said the plan differs materially from 2020, and moved to approve while agreeing EDR should supply a breakdown for the file.

cases.name: Award of Bids for Highway Materials
cases.summary: On a request from Highway General Foreman Jamie Norris, the board awarded annual bids for highway materials laid in place — asphalt milling/disposal, concrete, winter highway materials, aggregate stone, guardrails, catch basins and pavement markings — and authorized the Supervisor to sign. Described as routine annually bid items; adopted on a voice vote.

cases.name: Town Pool Concession Services — R&A Ice Cream (2025 Season)
cases.summary: The board approved a proposal from R&A Ice Cream to operate the town pool concession for the 2025 season and authorized the Supervisor to sign. Members discussed upcoming pool capital work — deck replacement and gutter/filter/pump improvements to be bid via KSCJ and Macri and performed after the season — and confirmed the pool remains on schedule to open on time. Adopted on a voice vote.

cases.name: KSCJ Engineering Services — Clove Road Baseball Fields
cases.address: 10 Clove Road / Corporate Clove Road, North White Plains, NY
cases.summary: The board approved a KSCJ proposal for engineering services for the baseball fields at Clove Road and authorized the Supervisor to sign. The Supervisor thanked applicant Bob Kandria for his patience and credited cost-saving collaboration with DeRosa Sports and Kellard's Joe Chimelli, noting drainage improvements and the possibility of reusing turf-project spoil material from Community Park to lower costs. Adopted on a voice vote; work anticipated to begin by the end of the season.
cases.publicComment: Applicant Bob Kandria attended and thanked the board for moving the long-delayed project forward.

memberPositions.evidence: Enthusiastically moved approval, thanked the applicant for persistence, and highlighted creative cost-saving measures and drainage improvements.

cases.name: Resignation — Austin Farkas, Building Maintenance Department
cases.summary: The board accepted a letter of resignation from Austin Farkas of the building maintenance department, effective April 11, 2025. Members praised him as an exceptional employee in the newly formed maintenance department who left for the private sector, and noted resumes for a replacement are already coming in. Adopted on a voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Praised Farkas as an exceptional employee and noted the town is working to fill the vacancy.

cases.name: Reappointment — Craig Benedict to the Conservation Board
cases.summary: The board reappointed Craig Benedict to the Conservation Board for a two-year term ending April 23, 2027. Members described him as an experienced and important member of the board. Adopted on a voice vote.

memberPositions.evidence: Gladly moved the reappointment, saying Benedict brings a lot of experience to an important board.

cases.name: Liaison Updates — Townwide Cleanup Day and Crosswalk Requests
cases.summary: In liaison updates, Councilwoman DiGiacinto detailed the townwide cleanup weekend logistics (orange bags, safety, no separate recyclables), a Westchester County free-compost event, and requests from senior residents for two new crosswalks — one by Hergenhan Center and one on Old Route 22 near the Beehive/affordable housing. The board discussed the Old Route 22 crosswalk's engineering and property complications (an ADA ramp landing on Beehive property) and agreed to have the Administrator, Police Chief/traffic sergeant and Town Planner study it. No formal action taken.

memberPositions.evidence: Led cleanup-day logistics and raised senior residents' requests for two new crosswalks, urging the board to figure out how to proceed.
Previously asked to examine whether the Old Route 22 crosswalk location was appropriate and whether it would benefit one side more than another.

Numerous bond, vehicle, highway, pool and engineering contracts approved, mostly routine.
Parking lot completion, ballfields, pool upgrades and wastewater plant advanced positively.
Recurring 'process first' theme drove tabling of the Mianus fee waiver pending a policy.
Invasive-vine program, cleanup day and wetland bonds well received.
250th-anniversary focus; Rochambeau membership rejected in favor of a town marker.
Hotel-tax home rule, under-budget purchases, cost scrutiny on the EDR increase.
Subdivision easements/bonds, equestrian special-use permit and wetland projects.

Advised on the negotiated cemetery-access easement scope, required the planning/county referrals and lead-agency declaration for the Cassone permit, addressed prior nonprofit fee-waiver history, and advised against conditionally issuing the EDR amendment.

Water/Sewer superintendent; delivered a detailed presentation justifying the EDR wastewater-plant redesign and cost increase, and confirmed the water/sewer truck purchases were budgeted and under budget.

Town Planner; clarified that Mianus River Gorge sought only a filing-fee waiver (not escrow) and was directed to develop a townwide nonprofit fee-waiver policy for the board.

meetings.attributionNote: The Supervisor (Joseph Rende) presides and is clearly identifiable as the presiding voice. Jose Berra is reliably identifiable via the chair addressing him by name ('What page are you on, Jose?'; 'Jose, you would like a breakdown') on the easements and EDR items. Barbara DiGiacinto is identifiable by the 'Barbara' address and as the sole woman (fee-waiver policy stance, cleanup update, reading the obituary). Saleem Hussain is referenced on the crosswalk-location question. Matt Milim spoke little and could not be confidently attributed a substantive stance beyond a procedural question.
